easy.q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
easy.exp: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with Chanakya's guidance.

easy.q: In which year did India gain independence?
easy.exp: India gained independence on 15 August 1947.

easy.q: Who wrote 'The Discovery of India'?
easy.exp: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote it in Ahmednagar jail in 1944.

easy.q: Ashoka embraced Buddhism after which battle?
easy.qt: அசோகர் எந்த போருக்கு பின் பௌத்தம் ஏற்றார்?
easy.exp: The Kalinga War (261 BCE) devastated Ashoka, leading him to embrace Buddhism.

easy.q: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
easy.exp: Shah Jahan built it as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal, completed ~1648 CE.

easy.q: Who launched the Quit India Movement in 1942?
easy.exp: Gandhi launched it on 8 August 1942 at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Mumbai.

easy.q: The Battle of Plassey was fought in:
easy.exp: Fought 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company and Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah.

easy.q: The first President of India was:
easy.exp: Dr Rajendra Prasad served as first President from 1950 to 1962.

easy.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
easy.exp: INC was founded on 28 December 1885 by A.O. Hume in Bombay.

easy.q: The first Battle of Panipat was fought in:
easy.exp: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526, establishing the Mughal Empire.

easy.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
easy.exp: General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful crowd on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar.

easy.q: Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in:
easy.exp: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

easy.q: The Dandi March took place in:
easy.exp: Gandhi's Salt March began 12 March 1930 and ended 6 April 1930, covering 241 miles.

easy.q: Who gave the slogan 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom'?
easy.qt: 'என் இரத்தம் தாருங்கள், சுதந்திரம் தருகிறேன்' என்று கூறியவர்?
easy.exp: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose gave this slogan to motivate Indians to join the INA.

easy.q: The partition of India and Pakistan occurred in:
easy.exp: Partition based on the Mountbatten Plan took place on 14-15 August 1947.

easy.q: Tipu Sultan was the ruler of:
easy.exp: Tipu Sultan (Tiger of Mysore) ruled Mysore and died fighting the British in 1799.

easy.q: Simon Commission came to India in:
easy.exp: Simon Commission arrived February 1928 and was boycotted as it had no Indian members.

easy.q: The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 began at:
easy.exp: The Revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857 over the greased cartridges issue.

easy.q: Who gave the title 'Mahatma' to Gandhi?
easy.exp: Rabindranath Tagore gave the title 'Mahatma' (Great Soul) to Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi.

easy.q: Who was the founder of the Sikh religion?
easy.exp: Guru Nanak (1469–1539) founded Sikhism and was the first of ten Sikh Gurus.

easy.q: The Indus Valley Civilization flourished approximately:
easy.exp: The civilization peaked around 2500-2000 BCE in the Indus River valley.

easy.q: Who was known as 'Punjab Kesari'?
easy.exp: Lala Lajpat Rai died from police lathi blows during protests against the Simon Commission in 1928.

easy.q: The Battle of Buxar was fought in:
easy.exp: Battle of Buxar (1764) was a decisive British victory consolidating power in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

easy.q: Who established the Vijayanagara Empire?
easy.exp: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE near Hampi.

easy.q: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj?
easy.exp: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Samaj in 1828, campaigning against sati and child marriage.

easy.q: Gandhiji was born in:
easy.exp: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.

easy.q: The Rowlatt Act was passed in:
easy.exp: Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed imprisonment without trial, sparking massive protests by Gandhi.

easy.q: Who was the last Mughal Emperor?
easy.exp: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal Emperor, exiled to Rangoon after the 1857 Revolt.

easy.q: The Chola dynasty was famous for its:
easy.exp: Chola dynasty (9th–13th c.) was famous for magnificent bronze sculptures (Nataraja) and naval power.

easy.q: The first Governor-General of India was:
easy.exp: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773.

easy.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
easy.exp: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister, serving from 1947 until his death in 1964.

easy.q: The 'Poona Pact' (1932) was signed between:
easy.exp: The Poona Pact was signed between Gandhi (who was on hunger strike) and B.R. Ambedkar regarding separate electorates for depressed classes.

easy.q: Who is called the 'Iron Man of India'?
easy.exp: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is called the 'Iron Man of India' for unifying the 562 princely states into the Indian Union.

easy.q: Vasco da Gama first arrived in India in:
easy.exp: Vasco da Gama first arrived at Kozhikode (Calicut), Kerala on 20 May 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India.

easy.q: The 'Cabinet Mission' came to India in:
easy.exp: The Cabinet Mission (1946) proposed a united India with federal structure, but it was eventually rejected.

easy.q: The Revolt of 1857 is also called:
easy.exp: V.D. Savarkar called the Revolt of 1857 the 'First War of Indian Independence'. The British called it 'Sepoy Mutiny'.

easy.q: Who designed the Indian National Flag?
easy.exp: Pingali Venkaiah designed the Indian National Flag. The final version was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947.

easy.q: The 'Servants of India Society' was founded by:
easy.exp: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 to train workers for national service.

medium.q:
Which of the following about the Indus Valley Civilization is/are correct?
1. Worshipped male and female deities.
2. Used horse-drawn chariots in warfare.
3. Cotton used for textiles.
medium.qt:
சிந்து வெளி நாகரிகம்:
1. ஆண், பெண் தெய்வங்கள் வழிபட்டனர்.
2. குதிரை ரதங்கள் பயன்படுத்தினர்.
3. பருத்தி நெசவுக்கு பயன்பட்டது.
medium.exp: Worshipped both (✓). Cotton textiles (✓). No evidence of horse chariots in Indus civilization (✗).
Lord Wellesley introduced Subsidiary Alliance in 1798, forcing Indian rulers to accept British troops.

medium.q: Who among these was NOT a Bhakti movement saint?
medium.exp: Shankaracharya (8th c.) propagated Advaita Vedanta — he predated the Bhakti movement.

medium.q: The Ghadar Party was founded in:
medium.qt: கதர் கட்சி நிறுவப்பட்ட இடம் மற்றும் ஆண்டு?
medium.exp: Ghadar Party was founded in San Francisco in 1913 by Lala Har Dayal.

medium.q: Correct chronological order: 1-Plassey  2-1857 Revolt  3-INC formation  4-Partition of Bengal
medium.exp: Plassey 1757 → Revolt 1857 → INC 1885 → Partition of Bengal 1905.
Rajendra Chola I (1014–1044 CE) conquered Ceylon and expanded the empire to Southeast Asia.

opts: A new syncretic religion he founded
medium.exp: Din-i-Ilahi (1582) was a syncretic religion combining Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, and Christianity.

medium.q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between:
medium.exp: The Marathas were decisively defeated by Ahmad Shah Durrani (Abdali) in 1761.

medium.q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was used by:
medium.exp: Lord Dalhousie (1848–56) used Doctrine of Lapse to annex Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, and others.
Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in 1875, promoting Vedic learning and opposing idol worship.

medium.q: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India was at:
medium.exp: Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar protested against the forced indigo cultivation system.

medium.q: The Permanent Settlement (1793) was introduced by:
medium.exp: Lord Cornwallis introduced Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa.

medium.q: The Khilafat Movement was launched to support:
medium.exp: Khilafat Movement (1919–24) by Ali Brothers supported the Ottoman Caliphate against British policies.

medium.q: The Home Rule League was founded by:
medium.exp: Two Home Rule Leagues were founded in 1916 — Tilak's in Pune, Annie Besant's in Madras.

medium.q: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
medium.exp: Dadabhai Naoroji (1825–1917) was the first Indian elected to British Parliament and propounded the 'Drain Theory'.

medium.q: Which Gupta ruler is called the 'Napoleon of India'?
medium.exp: Samudragupta (335–375 CE) is called the 'Napoleon of India' by historian V.A. Smith.

medium.q: Cripps Mission came to India in:
medium.exp: Cripps Mission (March 1942) proposed dominion status after WWII — rejected by both INC and Muslim League.

medium.q: Who established the Indian National Army (INA)?
medium.exp: Subhas Chandra Bose reorganized and led the INA (Azad Hind Fauj) from 1943 with Japanese support.
Lucknow Pact (1916) was signed between INC and All India Muslim League for joint action against the British.
Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims — a key step toward communal politics.
Lord William Bentinck abolished Sati by Regulation XVII in 1829, following Ram Mohan Roy's campaign.
Dadabhai Naoroji showed in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) how British rule drained India's wealth.

medium.q: The Vernacular Press Act was passed by:
medium.exp: Lord Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act in 1878 to muzzle Indian-language press. Repealed by Ripon in 1882.
Muhammad Ali Jinnah propounded the two-nation theory — Hindus and Muslims as separate nations — leading to partition.

medium.q: The Battle of Talikota (1565) resulted in:
medium.exp: Deccan Sultanate coalition defeated Vijayanagara; capital Hampi was destroyed and the empire rapidly declined.

medium.q: Who wrote 'Indica', the Greek account of Mauryan India?
medium.qt: மௌரிய இந்தியாவை பற்றிய கிரேக்க நூல் 'இண்டிகா' ஆசிரியர்?
medium.exp: Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador at Chandragupta Maurya's court and authored 'Indica'.

medium.q:
The Bhakti Movement in Tamil Nadu — which are correct?
1. Nayanmars were Shaivite devotees.
2. Alvars were Vaishnava devotees.
3. Their verses form Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
medium.qt:
1. நாயன்மார்கள் சைவர்கள்.
2. ஆழ்வார்கள் வைஷ்ணவர்கள்.
3. நாலாயிர திவ்ய பிரபந்தம்.
medium.exp: All correct. 63 Nayanmars (Shiva), 12 Alvars (Vishnu), 4000 verses of Alvars = Nalayira Divya Prabandham.

medium.q: Gandhiji's Champaran Movement (1917) was related to:
medium.exp: Champaran Satyagraha protested the forced indigo cultivation (tinkathia system) imposed by British planters.

medium.q: The 'Ryotwari Settlement' was a direct settlement between:
medium.exp: Ryotwari (introduced by Thomas Munro in Madras) was a direct settlement between the colonial government and individual peasants.

medium.q: The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) was primarily caused by:
opts: Zamindari exploitation and British land laws
medium.exp: The Santhal Rebellion was caused by exploitation by zamindars, moneylenders, and unjust British land settlement displacing tribals.

medium.q: The 'Mahad Satyagraha' (1927) was led by B.R. Ambedkar to assert the right of:
opts: Dalit access to a public tank (water source)
medium.exp: Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha in 1927 to assert the right of untouchables to draw water from the Chowdar Tank in Mahad, Maharashtra.

medium.q: The 'Divide and Rule' policy in India refers to:
opts: British strategy of creating divisions between communities to maintain control
medium.exp: 'Divide and Rule' was the British colonial strategy of deliberately creating and exploiting communal, caste, and regional divisions to prevent unified opposition.

medium.q:
Arrange these reform movements chronologically:
1. Brahmo Samaj  2. Arya Samaj  3. Ramakrishna Mission  4. Theosophical Society
medium.qt: காலவரிசைப்படி: 1. பிரம்ம சமாஜ் 2. ஆர்ய சமாஜ் 3. ராமகிருஷ்ண மிஷன் 4. தியோசாஃபிகல் சொசைட்டி
medium.exp: Brahmo Samaj (1828) → Arya Samaj (1875) → Theosophical Society in India (1882) → Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced Dyarchy — some subjects transferred to elected Indian ministers, others reserved for the Governor.

Gandhi's Eleven Vows included Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Brahmacharya (celibacy), Asteya (non-stealing), Aparigraha (non-possession), Sharirshrama (bread labour), Aswada, Sarvatra Bhayavarjana, Sarva Dharma Samanatva, Swadeshi, Sparshbhavana.

medium.q: The 'Vande Mataram' song is from which literary work?
medium.exp: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankimchandra Chatterjee in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882). First sung at INC session in 1896.
Swadeshi Movement (1905-08) was triggered by the partition of Bengal. Indians boycotted British goods and promoted Indian-made products.

medium.q: The 'Lucknow Session of INC' (1916) was significant because:
opts: Lucknow Pact between INC and Muslim League was signed
medium.exp: The 1916 Lucknow Session was significant because of the Lucknow Pact between INC and Muslim League, and Tilak's return to INC.

medium.q: Who was the Viceroy when India gained independence?
medium.exp: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India (1947). He oversaw the partition and independence of India and Pakistan.

medium.q: The 'Quit India Resolution' was passed at:
medium.exp: The Quit India Resolution was passed at the AICC session in Bombay (Mumbai) on 8 August 1942.

medium.q: The 'Indian Independence Act 1947' was passed by the British Parliament on:
medium.qt: 'இந்திய சுதந்திர சட்டம் 1947' பிரிட்டிஷ் நாடாளுமன்றத்தில் நிறைவேற்றப்பட்ட தேதி?
medium.exp: The Indian Independence Act 1947 was passed by British Parliament on 18 July 1947. It provided for the creation of two independent dominions — India and Pakistan — from 15 August 1947.

medium.q: Who was the first woman President of Indian National Congress?
medium.qt: இந்திய தேசிய காங்கிரஸின் முதல் பெண் தலைவர்?
medium.exp: Annie Besant became the first woman President of INC in 1917.

opts: Separate electorates for Harijans as originally proposed
Reserved seats in general (joint) electorates instead of separate electorates for depressed classes
medium.exp: Poona Pact replaced the Communal Award's separate electorates for depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates, preventing communal division of Hindu society.

opts: British trade restrictions and revenue policies in Bengal
medium.exp: The Sanyasi Rebellion in Bengal (1763-1800) was by wandering Hindu monks (sanyasis) and fakirs against British trade restrictions and revenue policies that caused food shortages.

opts: Bring the East India Company under Parliamentary control
medium.exp: Regulating Act 1773 was Britain's first step to regulate the East India Company — creating the post of Governor-General and a Supreme Court.
Gandhi wrote 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule) in 1909, articulating his vision of Indian self-rule based on moral regeneration.
The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected its President on 11 December 1946.
Kheda Satyagraha (1918) demanded revenue exemption for Gujarat farmers hit by crop failure and plague. Gandhi's support established his national stature.

opts: Tolerance, non-violence, moral conduct, respect for all religions
medium.exp: Ashoka's Dhamma was a moral code emphasizing tolerance, non-violence, respect for all sects, care for humans and animals, and righteous conduct — not Buddhist dogma per se.

medium.q: The 'Bengal Famine' of 1943 was primarily caused by:
opts: War-time policies, hoarding, and Bengal's rice exports to military — deliberate policy failure
medium.exp: The Bengal Famine (1943) killed 2-3 million people — caused by WWII war-time policies (rice denial to prevent Japanese use), exports, speculation, and hoarding. Churchill's policies are considered a major cause.

medium.q: 'Ashoka Stambha' (Pillar Edict) at Sarnath is the source of India's:
medium.exp: India's National Emblem is derived from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath — adopted on 26 January 1950. It shows four lions on an Abacus with a Dharma Chakra.

opts: Established by British; Indians were barred until 1864; Satyendranath Tagore was first Indian to pass
medium.exp: ICS was established by the British. The covenanted civil service was initially closed to Indians. Satyendranath Tagore (Rabindranath Tagore's brother) was the first Indian to pass the ICS exam in 1864.

hard.q: To convert a Saka Era year to CE, add:
hard.qt: சக சகாப்தத்திலிருந்து கி.பி.ஆக மாற்ற எத்தனை ஆண்டுகள் கூட்ட வேண்டும்?
hard.exp: Saka Era began 78 CE. Add 78 to convert. Important for reading ancient inscriptions.

hard.q: Pairs: 1-Kalhana→Rajatarangini  2-Barani→Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi  3-Abu'l-Fazl→Ain-i-Akbari. Correctly matched?
hard.exp: All correct. Kalhana (Kashmir history), Barani (Firuz Shah's reign), Abu'l-Fazl (Akbar's admin account).

hard.q:
Charvaka philosophy — which are correct?
1. Accepted Vedas as authority.
2. Pleasure is ultimate goal.
3. Rejected soul's existence.
hard.qt:
1. வேதங்களை ஆதாரமாக ஏற்றது.
2. இன்பம் வாழ்வின் இலக்கு.
3. ஆன்மாவின் இருப்பை மறுத்தது.
hard.exp: Charvaka REJECTED Vedas (1 wrong). Believed in pleasure as goal (✓). Denied eternal soul (✓).

hard.q:
Mansabdari system — which is correct?
1. Mansab denoted military rank and civil status.
2. Zat rank = cavalry to maintain.
3. Sawar rank = personal rank.
hard.qt:
1. மன்சப் இராணுவ மற்றும் சிவில் தரத்தை குறித்தது.
2. ஜாட் = குதிரைவீரர் எண்ணிக்கை.
3. சவார் = தனிப்பட்ட தரம்.
hard.exp: Zat = personal rank; Sawar = cavalry rank. Statements 2 and 3 are reversed. Only Statement 1 is correct.

hard.q: 'Home Charges' in British India referred to:
opts: India's payments to Britain for civil/military expenses
hard.exp: Home Charges = annual payments by India to Britain for admin, military costs, debt interest — key part of Drain of Wealth.

hard.q: The Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) is significant because:
opts: Exposed racial discrimination; mobilised Indian opinion
hard.exp: European fierce opposition to Indian judges trying Europeans exposed racism and united Indians — contributing to INC formation in 1885.

hard.q:
Uprising-Leader pairs:
1. Santhal Rebellion — Sidhu and Kanhu
2. Moplah Rebellion — Mambaram Tangal
3. Indigo Revolt — Bishnucharan Biswas
hard.exp: Santhal: Sidhu and Kanhu (✓). Indigo: Bishnucharan Biswas (✓). Moplah (1921): Ali Musaliar, not Mambaram Tangal.

hard.q:
Sufism in medieval India — which are correct?
1. Khanqah = Sufi hospice.
2. Chishti order emphasised poverty, rejected royal patronage.
3. Silsila = spiritual lineage.
hard.qt:
1. கான்காஹ் = ஆன்மீக மையம்.
2. சிஷ்டி வழிமுறை வறுமையை வலியுறுத்தியது.
3. சில்சிலா = ஆன்மீக வம்சாவழி.
hard.exp: All three correct. Khanqah (✓). Chishti poverty/no royal patronage (✓). Silsila = chain/lineage (✓).

hard.q: Arrange: 1-Regulating Act  2-Pitt's India Act  3-Charter Act 1833  4-Govt of India Act 1858
hard.exp: Regulating Act (1773) → Pitt's India Act (1784) → Charter Act (1833) → Govt of India Act (1858).

hard.q: Which of these was NOT part of Gandhi's 'Constructive Programme'?
hard.exp: Boycott was part of Non-Cooperation/Swadeshi — not Constructive Programme. CP included Khadi, sanitation, unity, women's uplift.

hard.q:
The 'Devadasi system' — which is/are correct?
1. Prevalent only in South India.
2. Associated with temple worship.
3. British first legislated against it.
hard.qt:
1. தென்னிந்தியாவில் மட்டும்.
2. கோயில் வழிபாட்டுடன் தொடர்புடையது.
3. பிரிட்டிஷரே முதல் சட்டம்.
hard.exp: Practiced across India not just South (1 wrong). Associated with temple worship (✓). Princely states first legislated, not British directly (3 wrong). Only 2 is correct.

hard.q:
The 'Permanent Settlement' (1793) — which are correct?
1. Created hereditary zamindars as landowners.
2. Revenue was permanently fixed.
3. Introduced in all provinces of British India.
hard.qt: 1. वंशानुगत जमींदार उत्पन्न किए। 2. राजस्व स्थायी रूप से तय किया। 3. सभी प्रांतों में लागू।
hard.exp: Permanent Settlement created hereditary zamindars (✓) and fixed revenue permanently (✓). But it was introduced only in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa — NOT all provinces (3 wrong).

hard.q: 'Swaraj Party' was founded in 1923 by:
hard.exp: Swaraj Party was founded by Motilal Nehru and C.R. (Chitta Ranjan) Das in 1923 to contest elections and obstruct the legislative councils from within.

hard.q: The 'August Offer' (1940) by Lord Linlithgow proposed:
opts: Dominion status after WWII + Indian participation in war council
hard.exp: The August Offer (8 Aug 1940) promised Dominion status after WWII, expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council to include more Indians, and establishment of a war advisory council — rejected by Congress.

easy.q: Which Article abolishes untouchability?
easy.exp: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

easy.q: The Preamble was amended by which Amendment?
easy.exp: 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

easy.q: Right to Education (Art 21A) was inserted by:
easy.exp: 86th Amendment Act (2002) inserted Art 21A — free compulsory education for children 6-14 years.

easy.q: Judicial Review is borrowed from:
easy.exp: Judicial Review (courts reviewing laws against the Constitution) is borrowed from the USA.

easy.q: How many Fundamental Duties?
easy.exp: Originally 10 duties (42nd Amendment 1976); an 11th added by 86th Amendment (2002).

easy.q: The Constitution came into force on:
easy.exp: Adopted 26 November 1949; came into force 26 January 1950 — celebrated as Republic Day.

easy.q: Father of the Indian Constitution:
easy.exp: Dr B.R. Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee — called Father of the Constitution.

easy.q: Article 32 is related to:
easy.exp: Art 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) allows moving SC directly for Fundamental Rights. Ambedkar called it 'heart and soul'.

easy.q: DPSP are contained in which Part?
easy.exp: DPSP are in Part IV of the Constitution (Articles 36-51).

easy.q: Rajya Sabha is a:
easy.exp: Rajya Sabha is a permanent House — it cannot be dissolved. One-third retire every two years.

easy.q: Total Lok Sabha seats (elected):
easy.exp: Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats.

easy.q: RTI Act was passed in:
easy.qt: தகவல் அறியும் உரிமை சட்டம் இயற்றப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
easy.exp: Right to Information (RTI) Act was passed in 2005.

easy.q: Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
easy.exp: CJI is appointed by the President under Art 124(2), conventionally on the outgoing CJI's recommendation.

easy.q: Minimum age for Rajya Sabha membership:
easy.exp: Minimum age for Rajya Sabha is 30 years (Article 84).

easy.q: Anti-Defection Law is in which Schedule?
easy.qt: கட்சி தாவல் தடை சட்டம் எந்த அட்டவணையில்?
easy.exp: Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment 1985) contains the Anti-Defection Law.

easy.q: Finance Commission is constituted under Article:
easy.exp: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, constituted by the President every five years.

easy.q: Oath to President is administered by:
easy.exp: CJI (or senior-most available judge) administers the oath to the President under Article 60.

easy.q: Lok Sabha quorum is:
easy.exp: Quorum = 1/10th of total membership (55 members).

easy.q: Election Commission was established in:
easy.exp: Election Commission established 25 January 1950 under Article 324.

easy.q: Article 21 deals with:
opts: Right to Life and Personal Liberty
easy.exp: Art 21: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law.

easy.q: Languages in the 8th Schedule:
easy.exp: Currently 22 officially recognised languages in the Eighth Schedule.

easy.q: Emergency under Article 356 is known as:
easy.exp: Article 356 provides for President's Rule (State Emergency) when state constitutional machinery fails.

easy.q: Right to Property was removed from FDRs by:
easy.exp: 44th Amendment (1978) removed Right to Property from FDRs and made it a legal right under Art 300A.

easy.q: Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by:
easy.exp: Speaker is elected by Lok Sabha members from among themselves (Article 93).

easy.q: Governor of a State is appointed by:
easy.exp: Governor is appointed by the President under Article 155.

easy.q: Money Bills can be introduced only in:
easy.exp: Money Bills (Article 110) can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.

easy.q: Article 72 deals with:
easy.exp: Art 72: President can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions — including in death sentence cases.

easy.q: Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in:
easy.qt: திட்டக் கமிஷன் NITI ஆயோக்காக மாற்றப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
easy.exp: NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

easy.q: Maximum gap between two Parliamentary sessions:
easy.qt: இரண்டு நாடாளுமன்ற கூட்டங்களுக்கு இடையேயான அதிகபட்ச இடைவெளி?
easy.exp: Article 85: no more than 6 months between two parliamentary sessions.

easy.q: Minimum age to become President of India:
easy.exp: Minimum age to become President: 35 years (Article 58).

medium.q:
DPSP statements:
1. Justiciable.
2. Part IV (Art 36-51).
3. Aim at welfare state.
medium.qt:
DPSP:
1. நீதியில் நடைமுறைப்படுத்தலாம்.
2. பகுதி IV (36-51).
3. நல அரசு நோக்கம்.
medium.exp: DPSPs are non-justiciable (1 wrong). In Part IV Art 36-51 (✓). Aim at welfare state (✓).
Public Order (Entry 1) is a State List subject.
73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj, adding Part IX and 11th Schedule.

medium.qt: குடியரசுத் தலைவரை பதவி நீக்கம் செய்யும் சட்டப்பிரிவு?
medium.exp: Article 61 provides the procedure for impeachment of the President.
Estimates Committee examines future estimates; PAC examines past expenditure.

medium.q: Writ that orders a public authority to perform a duty:
medium.exp: Mandamus ('we command') orders a public official to perform a mandatory duty they failed to perform.
Zero Hour starts at 12 noon — MPs raise urgent matters without prior notice. Not mentioned in Constitution.
Kesavananda Bharati v Kerala (1973) — SC held Parliament cannot amend the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.

medium.q: Fundamental Duties were added by the:
medium.exp: 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Art 51A) based on Swaran Singh Committee.
Arts 25-28: Right to Freedom of Religion — conscience, manage religious affairs, no tax for religion, no religious instruction in state schools.

medium.q: New states can be created by Parliament under:
medium.qt: புதிய மாநிலங்கள் நாடாளுமன்றத்தால் எந்த சட்டப்பிரிவின் கீழ் உருவாக்கப்படும்?
medium.exp: Article 3 empowers Parliament (by simple majority) to create new states, alter boundaries and names.

medium.q: Residuary powers in India belong to:
medium.exp: Unlike USA (residuary to states), in India residuary powers belong to the Union/Parliament.

medium.q: CAG of India is appointed by:
medium.exp: CAG appointed by President under Art 148. Audits all government accounts.
VP elected by members of both Houses of Parliament assembled in a joint meeting (Art 66).

medium.q: Article 3 vs Article 368 — creating a new state requires:
medium.qt: புதிய மாநிலம் உருவாக்க Art 3 vs Art 368?
opts: Simple majority of Parliament + Presidential assent
medium.exp: Art 3 requires only a simple majority in Parliament + Presidential assent (not special majority under Art 368). States' consent is not required.
74th Amendment gave constitutional status to municipalities, adding Part IX-A and 12th Schedule.

opts: Legislature doing indirectly what it cannot do directly
medium.exp: Prevents a legislature from encroaching on another's jurisdiction by framing a law differently.

medium.q: National Emergency (Art 352) can be proclaimed due to:
opts: War, external aggression, or armed rebellion
medium.exp: Art 352 covers war, external aggression, or armed rebellion (44th Amendment changed 'internal disturbance' to 'armed rebellion').

medium.q: Cultural and Educational Rights of minorities (Arts 29-30):
medium.exp: Art 29: conserve language/culture. Art 30: minorities' right to establish and administer educational institutions.

medium.q: The President can issue ordinances when:
medium.qt: குடியரசுத் தலைவர் அவசர ஆணை பிறப்பிக்கும் நேரம்?
medium.exp: Under Art 123, President can issue ordinances only when both Houses are not in session.

opts: Tribal areas administration in NE India
medium.exp: 6th Schedule: administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram through Autonomous District Councils.

medium.q: High Court judges are appointed by:
opts: President in consultation with CJI and Governor
medium.exp: HC judges appointed by President under Art 217 in consultation with CJI and concerned state Governor.

medium.q: India follows which type of government?
medium.exp: India follows Parliamentary (Westminster) system — executive responsible to legislature.
Habeas Corpus ('you may have the body') directs authorities to produce a detained person before court.
Question Hour = first hour of every Parliamentary sitting where ministers answer members' questions.

opts: Restored rights curtailed by 42nd Amendment; amended Emergency provisions
medium.exp: 44th Amendment (1978) restored several rights curtailed by 42nd Amendment and added emergency safeguards.

medium.q: The SC's 'Constitutional Morality' principle was invoked in:
medium.exp: Navtej Singh Johar v Union of India (2018) — decriminalised consensual homosexuality — extensively invoked constitutional morality.

opts: Quash the order of a lower court acting beyond jurisdiction
medium.exp: Certiorari quashes the order of a lower court/tribunal that has acted beyond its jurisdiction or against principles of natural justice.

medium.q: The 'Doctrine of Ultra Vires' in constitutional law means:
medium.exp: Ultra Vires ('beyond powers') = an act performed by a body/authority that exceeds the powers granted to it by law or the Constitution.

medium.q: Under the Constitution, which is a 'state' for Art 12 (definition of state for Fundamental Rights)?
medium.qt: அடிப்படை உரிமைகளுக்கு சட்டப்பிரிவு 12 கீழ் 'மாநிலம்' என்பதில் அடங்குவது?
opts: Government of India, Parliament, State Govts, Local bodies + instrumentalities of State
medium.exp: Art 12: 'State' includes Government of India, Parliament, state governments and legislatures, and all local or other authorities under the control of the government or funded by it.

medium.q: The 'Panchayat Extension to Scheduled Areas' (PESA) Act 1996 extends:
opts: Panchayat Raj to all tribal areas
Gram Sabha powers to Schedule V areas, giving tribals self-governance
medium.exp: PESA (1996) extended Panchayati Raj provisions to Schedule V (tribal) areas in 10 states, empowering Gram Sabhas with self-governance, traditional rights, and control over resources.

medium.q: Which of the following has original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
opts: Disputes between the Union and one or more states
medium.exp: Under Art 131, SC has original jurisdiction in disputes between the Union and states, or between two or more states — exclusively. This cannot be heard by any other court.

medium.q: The President of India cannot dissolve:
medium.exp: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha but NOT the Rajya Sabha — as it is a permanent House. State Assemblies can be dissolved by the Governor on CM's advice.

medium.q: 'Comptroller and Auditor General' (CAG) — which is correct?
opts: CAG is the guardian of public purse; reports to Parliament; independent of Executive
medium.exp: CAG is the supreme audit institution — independent of executive, submits reports to Parliament/State Legislatures, and guards the public purse.

opts: Device to raise an urgent public issue by interrupting House business
medium.exp: Adjournment Motion is a device to draw attention to a definite matter of urgent public importance by adjourning business of the House — allowed only in Lok Sabha.

medium.q: 'Financial Emergency' under Art 360 can be proclaimed when:
opts: When financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened
medium.exp: Art 360: Financial Emergency when the financial stability or credit of India or any state is threatened. Never been proclaimed in India so far.

opts: Freedom of speech inside Parliament without liability in any court
medium.exp: Parliamentary privileges include freedom of speech inside Parliament (protected from court proceedings), right to publish debates, and right to punish outsiders for breach of privilege.

medium.q: The 'Right to Privacy' was declared a Fundamental Right by the SC in:
medium.qt: 'தனியுரிமை உரிமை' அடிப்படை உரிமை என தீர்ப்பளிக்கப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
medium.exp: In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017), a 9-judge SC bench unanimously held that Right to Privacy is a Fundamental Right under Art 21.

medium.q: The 'No-Confidence Motion' can be moved only in:
medium.exp: A No-Confidence Motion (censure motion against Council of Ministers) can only be moved in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.

medium.q: 'NOTA' (None of the Above) was introduced in Indian elections in:
medium.exp: NOTA was introduced in Indian elections in 2013 following the Supreme Court order in People's Union for Civil Liberties v Union of India (2013).
Gram Nyayalayas (village courts) were established under the Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008 to provide cheap and quick justice at grassroots level.

medium.q: 'Token Money Bill' vs 'Appropriation Bill' — which is correct?
medium.qt: 'டோக்கன் மணி பில்' vs 'திரும்பளிப்பு மசோதா' — சரியான விளக்கம்?
opts: Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from Consolidated Fund; token bills are for small grants in lieu
Token bills are for rural areas only
Appropriation Bill is only for defence
medium.exp: Appropriation Bill authorises the government to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund for approved expenditure. It gives formal legal authority to government spending.

medium.q: 'Comptroller' role of CAG differs from 'Auditor' role in that:
opts: Comptroller role (for Union) was eliminated; CAG now mainly audits state/central accounts
The Comptroller role was formally abandoned; CAG now mainly functions as auditor
Comptroller role applies to state governments only
medium.exp: CAG's comptroller function (pre-authorising government expenditure) was abolished in 1976 when the Consolidated Fund was changed. CAG now mainly functions as auditor, not pre-auditor.

opts: Division of taxing powers and expenditure responsibilities between Centre and States
medium.exp: Fiscal federalism = constitutional division of taxing powers (Union List, State List, concurrent) and expenditure responsibilities between Central and State governments, with Finance Commission managing transfers.

hard.q:
Constitutional language provisions:
1. Hindi in Devanagari = official Union language.
2. English only for 15 years.
3. States may adopt own language.
hard.qt:
1. தேவநாகரி இந்தி ஆட்சி மொழி.
2. ஆங்கிலம் 15 ஆண்டுகள் மட்டும்.
3. மாநிலங்கள் சொந்த மொழி ஏற்கலாம்.
hard.exp: All correct. Art 343: Hindi official. English extended indefinitely by Official Languages Act 1963. Art 345: states can adopt own language.

hard.q:
Governor's absolute discretionary powers:
1. Sending Art 356 report.
2. Reserving Bill for President.
3. Seeking info from CM.
4. Returning non-money bill.
hard.exp: Sending Art 356 report and reserving a Bill (Art 201) are absolute discretionary. Seeking info (Art 167) and returning bill are done on CM's advice.

hard.q:
9th Schedule:
1. Laws completely immune from judicial review.
2. Added by First Amendment.
3. IR Coelho case (2007): violations of basic structure can be reviewed.
hard.qt:
9வது அட்டவணை:
1. முழு நீதி மறுஆய்வு விலக்கு.
2. முதல் திருத்தத்தால் சேர்க்கப்பட்டது.
3. IR Coelho தீர்ப்பு: மறுஆய்வு சாத்தியம்.
hard.exp: 9th Schedule added by 1st Amendment (✓). IR Coelho (2007): laws after 24 April 1973 violating basic structure CAN be reviewed — NOT immune (1 wrong).

hard.q:
Article 356 safeguards:
1. Parliamentary approval within 2 months.
2. Extension beyond 1 year only if Emergency is in operation.
3. SR Bommai (1994): President's Rule subject to judicial review.
hard.qt:
1. 2 மாதத்தில் நாடாளுமன்றம் அங்கீகரிக்க வேண்டும்.
2. 1 ஆண்டுக்கு மேல் நீட்டிக்க அவசரநிலை தேவை.
3. SR Bommai: நீதி மறுஆய்வுக்கு உட்பட்டது.
hard.exp: All three correct. 2-month approval (44th Amendment). Beyond 1 year needs national emergency. SR Bommai (1994) made it judicially reviewable.

hard.q: Art 368 amendments affecting federal structure require:
hard.qt: சட்டப்பிரிவு 368 கீழ் கூட்டாட்சி கட்டமைப்பை பாதிக்கும் திருத்தங்களுக்கு?
opts: Special majority + ratification by at least half state legislatures
hard.exp: Federal structure amendments need special majority (2/3 of present and voting + majority of total membership) PLUS ratification by at least half state legislatures.

hard.q: Double jeopardy is protected under:
hard.exp: Art 20(2): no person can be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.

hard.q: Which are Constitutional Bodies (created directly by Constitution)?
opts: Election Commission, UPSC, CAG, Finance Commission
hard.exp: EC (Art 324), UPSC (Art 315), CAG (Art 148), Finance Commission (Art 280) — all constitutional. NHRC, CBI, SEBI are statutory.

hard.q: Maneka Gandhi case (1978) expanded Art 21 by holding:
hard.qt: மானேகா காந்தி வழக்கு (1978) சட்டப்பிரிவு 21 ஐ விரிவுபடுத்தியது எப்படி?
opts: Art 21 limited to mere physical existence
'Procedure established by law' must be just, fair, and reasonable
hard.exp: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India (1978) held that 'procedure established by law' must be just, fair, and reasonable — vastly expanding Art 21's scope.

hard.q: 'Minority' for Art 30 is determined:
hard.exp: Both religious and linguistic minorities have Art 30 rights. TMA Pai Foundation case (2002) clarified minority status is determined state-wise.

hard.q: Under Art 143, President can seek SC advisory opinion on:
hard.qt: சட்டப்பிரிவு 143 கீழ் குடியரசுத் தலைவர் SC ஆலோசனை கோரலாம்?
opts: Question of law or fact of public importance
hard.exp: Art 143 allows President to refer any question of law or fact of public importance to SC for advisory opinion.

hard.q:
Consolidated Fund of India — which are correct?
1. No money without Appropriation Act.
2. Includes revenues, loans, repayments.
3. CAG audits all expenditure from it.
hard.qt:
1. திரும்பளிப்பு சட்டம் இல்லாமல் பணம் எடுக்க முடியாது.
2. வருவாய், கடன்கள் அடங்கும்.
3. CAG தணிக்கை செய்யும்.
hard.exp: All three correct. Art 114: Appropriation Act needed. Art 266: includes revenues/loans. CAG audits all govt expenditure.

hard.q: Collegium system — which is correct?
opts: Government has final say on HC judge appointment
SC collegium recommendation is binding for SC judges
CJI alone decides all SC appointments
hard.exp: Second Judges Case (1993): collegium's recommendation is binding on the President for SC appointments.

hard.q:
73rd Amendment — which are mandatory?
1. Gram Sabha.
2. Three-tier structure.
3. SC/ST reservation proportional to population.
4. Five-year term.
hard.exp: All four are mandatory: Gram Sabha, three-tier structure, SC/ST reservations, and five-year term.

hard.q: Doctrine of Pleasure means:
opts: President acts at will without advice
Certain officials hold office at the President's pleasure
hard.exp: Art 310: certain high officials hold posts at pleasure of President/Governor — can be dismissed subject to constitutional safeguards.

easy.q: Highest peak entirely within India:
easy.qt: இந்தியாவிற்குள் மட்டுமே அமைந்த மிக உயரமான சிகரம்?
easy.exp: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) on Sikkim-Nepal border. K2 is in Pakistan-administered territory.

easy.q: Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
easy.exp: 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.

easy.q: 'Sorrow of Bihar' river:
easy.exp: Kosi River floods frequently due to heavy silt deposits that shift its course.

easy.q: Sundarbans is in:
easy.exp: Sundarbans — world's largest mangrove forest — is in West Bengal (also extends into Bangladesh).

easy.q: Longest river in India:
easy.exp: Ganga (2,525 km) is the longest river entirely in India.

easy.q: India's southernmost point:
easy.exp: Indira Point (Pygmalion Point) in Great Nicobar Island. Kanyakumari is the southernmost mainland point.

easy.q: Largest desert in India:
easy.exp: Thar Desert in Rajasthan is the largest desert in India, 7th largest in the world.

easy.q: State with longest coastline in India:
easy.exp: Gujarat has the longest coastline (~1,600 km).

easy.q: Western Ghats are also known as:
easy.exp: Western Ghats = Sahyadri range, running parallel to the western coast.

easy.q: Brahmaputra originates in:
easy.exp: Brahmaputra originates from Chemayungdung glacier near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet.

easy.q: Chilika Lake is in:
easy.exp: Chilika Lake in Odisha is Asia's largest brackish water lagoon and a Ramsar Wetland Site.

easy.q: Capital of Ladakh:
easy.exp: Leh is the capital of the Union Territory of Ladakh.

easy.q: Largest lake in India:
easy.exp: Vembanad Lake in Kerala is the longest lake; Wular Lake in J&K is the largest freshwater lake.

easy.q: Silent Valley National Park is in:
easy.exp: Silent Valley NP is in Palakkad district, Kerala — famous for undisturbed tropical rainforest.

easy.q: Indian Standard Time (IST) corresponds to which longitude?
easy.exp: IST corresponds to 82.5°E longitude, passing through Mirzapur, UP.

easy.q: The Sundarbans delta is formed by:
easy.exp: Sundarbans delta formed by Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers emptying into Bay of Bengal.

easy.q: Largest Union Territory of India by area:
easy.exp: Ladakh is the largest UT of India by area (59,146 sq km).

easy.q: Which river originates in Amarkantak?
easy.exp: Narmada River originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh.

easy.q: Palk Strait separates India from:
easy.qt: பால்க் நீர்ச்சந்தி இந்தியாவை எந்த நாட்டிலிருந்து பிரிக்கிறது?
easy.exp: Palk Strait separates southeastern India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka.

easy.q: Majuli island is in which river?
easy.exp: Majuli — world's largest river island — is in the Brahmaputra, Assam.

easy.q: Konkan Coast lies between:
easy.exp: Konkan Coast extends from Mumbai (Daman) to Goa along the western coast.

easy.q: City on the banks of Sabarmati:
easy.exp: Ahmedabad is on the Sabarmati River. Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram is here.

easy.q: Loktak Lake (NE India's largest freshwater lake) is in:
easy.exp: Loktak Lake in Manipur has floating 'phumdis' and the world's only floating national park.

easy.q: Eastern Ghats pass through:
easy.qt: கிழக்குத் தொடர்ச்சி மலை எந்த மாநிலங்கள் வழியாக?
easy.exp: Eastern Ghats are discontinuous ranges through Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha.

easy.q: State with maximum forest cover in India:
easy.qt: இந்தியாவில் மிக அதிக வனப்பகுதி கொண்ட மாநிலம்?
easy.exp: Arunachal Pradesh has maximum forest cover by area; Mizoram leads by percentage of total area.

easy.q: Nilgiris are at the junction of:
easy.exp: Nilgiri Hills are at the junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka.

easy.q: Coromandel Coast gets rainfall primarily during:
easy.qt: கோரமண்டல் கரை முக்கியமாக எப்போது மழை பெறுகிறது?
easy.exp: Coromandel Coast (east coast of TN and southern AP) gets most rain during the Northeast monsoon.

easy.q: Highest waterfall in India:
easy.exp: Kunchikal Falls in Karnataka (455 m) is the highest waterfall in India.

medium.q:
Western Ghats statements:
1. Older than Himalayas.
2. Parallel to western coast.
3. UNESCO Biodiversity Hotspot 2012.
medium.qt:
1. இமயமலையை விட பழமையானவை.
2. மேற்கு கரைக்கு இணையாக.
3. யுனெஸ்கோ 2012.
medium.exp: All correct. Ancient block mountains (Archean) > Himalayan age. Run parallel to west coast. UNESCO 2012.
Cauvery → Talakaveri, Coorg. Narmada → Amarkantak. Godavari → Trimbakeshwar. Krishna → Mahabaleshwar.
Bhabar = narrow gravel/pebble belt at Himalayan foothills. Rivers flow underground here, re-emerge in Terai.

medium.q: Indian monsoon is primarily caused by:
opts: Differential heating of land and sea; ITCZ shift
medium.exp: Indian monsoon caused by differential heating of land/sea, northward shift of ITCZ in summer, and Coriolis effect.

medium.q: Deccan Trap formation was caused by:
medium.exp: Deccan Traps formed by massive volcanic eruptions around 65 million years ago (end of Cretaceous).
Narmada, Tapi, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri are Peninsular rivers originating in the Deccan.

medium.q: Western Disturbances in India originate over:
medium.exp: Western Disturbances originate as extratropical cyclones over the Mediterranean Sea, bringing winter rain to NW India.

medium.q: Rain Shadow area of Western Ghats:
medium.exp: The Deccan Plateau (leeward/eastern side) is in the rain shadow — much drier than the windward western side.

medium.q: Soil best suited for cotton cultivation in India:
medium.qt: இந்தியாவில் பருத்தி சாகுபடிக்கு மிகவும் ஏற்ற மண் வகை?
medium.exp: Black soil (Regur) found in Deccan Plateau — high clay content, moisture retention — ideal for cotton.

medium.q: Kaziranga National Park is associated with:
medium.exp: Kaziranga NP in Assam is home to ~2/3 of world's Indian One-horned Rhinoceros. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Project Tiger launched 1 April 1973 by PM Indira Gandhi at Jim Corbett National Park.
Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (AP/Telangana) is largest by area (3,568 sq km).
The Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta is the world's largest river delta.
Chhota Nagpur Plateau (Jharkhand) — rich in coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite.

medium.qt: மிக உயரமான சிகரங்களை கொண்ட இமயமலைத் தொடர்?
medium.exp: Great Himalayas (Himadri) is northernmost and highest — contains Everest, Kangchenjunga, etc.
Terai = marshy, swampy lowland belt south of the Bhabar, at Himalayan foothills. Rich biodiversity.
Lakshadweep = coral atolls in the Arabian Sea. India's smallest UT with 36 islands.

medium.q: Malabar Coast refers to the coast of:
medium.exp: Malabar Coast = southwestern coast of India, primarily Kerala and parts of Karnataka.
India's EEZ extends 200 nautical miles from the baseline, giving sovereign rights over natural resources.

medium.q:
Indo-Gangetic Plain alluvium types:
1. Formed by Himalayan river deposits.
2. Bhangar and Khadar are two types.
3. Khadar is older; Bhangar is newer.
medium.qt:
1. ஹிமாலய நதிகளின் படிவால் உருவானது.
2. பங்கர் மற்றும் கதார் — இரண்டு வகைகள்.
3. கதார் பழைய வண்டல்; பங்கர் புதியது.
medium.exp: Formed by Himalayan rivers (✓). Bhangar and Khadar are alluvium types (✓). But Bhangar is OLD; Khadar is NEW — Statement 3 is reversed.

medium.q: Which soil has highest water retention?
medium.qt: மிக அதிக நீர் தேக்கும் திறன் கொண்ட மண் வகை?
medium.exp: Black cotton soil (Regur) has highest water retention — swells when wet, cracks when dry.

opts: Kerala, Karnataka, and parts of Maharashtra and Odisha
medium.exp: Laterite soil is found mainly in high rainfall areas with alternating wet and dry seasons — Kerala, Karnataka, parts of Maharashtra, Odisha, and some hill regions.
Blue Revolution refers to the development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in India, aiming to increase fish production.

medium.q: The 'Kaziranga' National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for which primary reason?
medium.qt: காஸிரங்கா தேசிய பூங்கா UNESCO அங்கீகாரம் பெற்ற முக்கிய காரணம்?
opts: Major population of Indian one-horned rhinoceros
medium.exp: Kaziranga NP was inscribed as UNESCO WHS in 1985 primarily for its extraordinary density of Indian one-horned rhinoceros (~2/3 of world population).

medium.q: Which is India's longest national highway?
medium.exp: NH-44 (formerly NH-7) from Srinagar to Kanyakumari is India's longest national highway at ~3,745 km.

medium.q: 'Project Snow Leopard' was launched to conserve:
opts: Snow leopards and their Himalayan/Trans-Himalayan habitat
medium.exp: Project Snow Leopard (2009) was launched to protect snow leopards and their Himalayan and Trans-Himalayan habitats in 5 states: J&K, HP, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh.

opts: They act as coastal protection, carbon sink, nursery for marine life
medium.exp: Mangroves protect coasts from storms and tsunamis, serve as carbon sinks, provide nursery habitats for marine species, and support coastal livelihoods.

medium.q: The 'Deccan plateau' is bounded on the north by:
medium.qt: டெக்கான் பீடபூமி வடக்கில் எந்த மலைத்தொடர்களால் எல்லையிடப்படுகிறது?
medium.exp: The Deccan Plateau is bounded on the north by the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

medium.q: India shares its longest border with which country?
medium.qt: இந்தியா மிக நீண்ட எல்லையை பகிர்ந்து கொள்ளும் நாடு?
medium.exp: India shares its longest border with Bangladesh (~4,156 km), followed by China (~3,488 km), Pakistan (~3,323 km), Nepal, and others.
National Waterway 1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system) extends from Haldia (Kolkata) to Allahabad (Prayagraj), total 1,620 km.

medium.q: The 'Andaman and Nicobar Islands' are separated from Thailand by:
medium.qt: அந்தமான் மற்றும் நிக்கோபார் தீவுகள் தாயிலாந்திலிருந்து பிரிக்கப்படுவது?
medium.exp: The Strait of Malacca separates the Andaman and Nicobar Islands from the Thai-Malay Peninsula in the east.
Jim Corbett National Park is in Uttarakhand — India's first national park (est. 1936 as Hailey NP, renamed after Jim Corbett in 1957).

medium.q: The Godavari River is also known as:
medium.qt: கோதாவரி நதி வேறு என்ன பெயரில் அழைக்கப்படுகிறது?
medium.exp: Godavari is called 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South) due to its importance in the Deccan region and its sacred status.

opts: Elevated sea surface temperatures causing coral to expel symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae)
medium.exp: Coral bleaching occurs primarily when sea surface temperatures rise above normal, causing coral polyps to expel their symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) — turning white. Prolonged bleaching causes coral death.
The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats converge at the Nilgiri Hills (Blue Mountains) in the corner of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala.

opts: Transporting heat from equatorial to polar regions, moderating coastal climates
Creating rainfall only in tropical areas
medium.exp: Ocean currents transport warm water from equatorial regions to polar regions and cold water back, moderating coastal climates — warm currents warm up cold coasts; cold currents cool warm coasts.
Teesta is a tributary of the Brahmaputra River. It flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before joining the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh.
Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is India's largest freshwater lake.

opts: Northeast India, Bhutan, Nepal, and Yunnan province of China
medium.exp: The Eastern Himalayas Biodiversity Hotspot covers northeast India (incl. all 8 NE states), Bhutan, Nepal, and parts of southern China (Yunnan).
Project Elephant was launched in 1992 by the Government of India to protect wild elephants, their habitats, and migration corridors.

opts: Compensatory Afforestation — funds collected when forest land is diverted for non-forest use
medium.exp: CAMPA (Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority) manages funds collected when forest land is diverted for development — to be used for afforestation elsewhere.

opts: Western Ghats and Indo-Burma; partially Sundaland and Eastern Himalayas
medium.exp: India has parts of 4 globally recognised biodiversity hotspots: Western Ghats (entirely), Indo-Burma hotspot (NE India), Eastern Himalayas, and Sundaland (Andaman & Nicobar).
Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary is in Rajasthan, surrounding the Kumbhalgarh Fort — habitat for wolves, leopards, sloth bears, and four-horned antelopes.

hard.q:
IOD (Indian Ocean Dipole) — which are correct?
1. Positive IOD → above-normal Indian rainfall.
2. Measures SST difference between western and eastern tropical Indian Ocean.
3. IOD always occurs with El Niño.
hard.qt:
1. நேர்மறை IOD — அதிக மழை.
2. கடல் வெப்பநிலை வேறுபாடு கிழக்கு-மேற்கு.
3. IOD எல்நீனோவுடன் எப்போதும் நிகழும்.
hard.exp: Positive IOD enhances Indian monsoon (✓). Measures eastern-western SST difference (✓). IOD and El Niño are independent (3 wrong).

hard.q: Consider: 1-Karakoram has K2  2-Ladakh Range north of Zaskar  3-Zaskar north of Great Himalayas. Correct?
hard.qt:
1. காரகோரமில் K2.
2. லடாக் தொடர் சன்ஸ்காருக்கு வடக்கில்.
3. சன்ஸ்கர் பெரிய இமயமலைக்கு வடக்கில்.
hard.exp: All three correct. K2 in Karakoram (✓). Order S→N: Great Himalayas→Zaskar→Ladakh→Karakoram. Ladakh north of Zaskar (✓). Zaskar north of Great Himalayas (✓).

hard.q: 'Roaring Forties', 'Furious Fifties', 'Screaming Sixties' refer to:
opts: Powerful westerly winds in Southern Ocean at those latitudes
hard.exp: These refer to powerful westerly wind belts in the Southern Ocean at 40°S, 50°S, 60°S — blowing unobstructed around Antarctica.

hard.q: North-East India receives very high rainfall primarily because:
hard.qt: வடகிழக்கு இந்தியா அதிக மழை பெறுவதற்கான முக்கிய காரணம்?
opts: Bay of Bengal monsoon branch + orographic lift from Meghalaya hills
hard.exp: Bay of Bengal monsoon branch + orographic lift at Khasi Hills (Cherrapunji/Mawsynram) = extremely heavy rainfall.

hard.q: 'Transpiration' in hydrological cycle refers to:
hard.exp: Transpiration = process by which plants release water vapour from leaves and stems.

hard.q: Western Disturbances primarily affect:
opts: Northwestern India — J&K, HP, Punjab, Uttarakhand
hard.exp: Western Disturbances bring winter rain/snow to NW India — J&K, HP, Punjab, Uttarakhand.

easy.q: Which body replaced the Planning Commission?
easy.exp: NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

easy.q: GST was implemented from:
easy.exp: GST implemented from 1 July 2017.

easy.q: Green Revolution mainly associated with:
easy.exp: Green Revolution (1960s-70s) = HYV seeds of Wheat and Rice.

easy.q: Stock market regulator in India:
easy.exp: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India, est. 1992) regulates the securities market.

easy.q: NABARD stands for:
opts: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
easy.exp: NABARD = National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, established 1982.

easy.q: RBI was established in:
easy.exp: RBI established 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act 1934; nationalised in 1949.

easy.q: 'Repo Rate' is the rate at which:
easy.exp: Repo Rate = rate at which RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities.

easy.q: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana aims at:
opts: Financial inclusion — bank accounts for all
easy.exp: PMJDY (launched 28 Aug 2014) provides zero-balance bank accounts for unbanked households.

easy.q: Largest commercial bank in India:
easy.exp: State Bank of India (SBI) is the largest public sector and commercial bank by assets, branches, employees.

easy.q: WTO headquarters is in:
easy.exp: WTO headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. India is a founding member (1995).

easy.q: GDP base year (current) in India:
easy.exp: India's current GDP base year is 2011-12 (revised from 2004-05 in 2015).

easy.q: MUDRA stands for:
opts: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency
easy.exp: MUDRA = Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency, providing loans up to ₹10 lakh for small businesses.

easy.q: India's First Five Year Plan was launched in:
easy.exp: First Five Year Plan (1951-56) focused on agriculture, based on Harrod-Domar model.

easy.q: World Bank headquarters:
easy.exp: World Bank Group is headquartered in Washington, D.C.

easy.q: GST has how many main tax slabs?
easy.exp: GST has 4 main tax slabs: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%.

easy.q: What is 'Inflation'?
easy.exp: Inflation = general, sustained increase in the price level, reducing purchasing power of money.

easy.q: SEBI was established in:
easy.exp: SEBI established as non-statutory in 1988; given statutory powers in 1992 under SEBI Act 1992.

easy.q: Fiscal Deficit is:
opts: Total government expenditure minus total revenue
easy.exp: Fiscal Deficit = Total expenditure - Total revenue (excluding borrowings). Indicates total borrowing requirement.

easy.q: MSP is fixed by:
easy.exp: MSP announced by GoI based on CACP recommendations, approved by CCEA.

easy.q: 'Priority Sector Lending' requires commercial banks to lend at least:
easy.exp: RBI mandates domestic commercial banks to lend at least 40% of ANBC to priority sectors.

easy.q: India's current GDP rank globally (approx):
easy.exp: India is the world's 5th largest economy by nominal GDP. By PPP, India is the 3rd largest.

easy.q: 'Gini Coefficient' measures:
easy.exp: Gini Coefficient measures income inequality — 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (maximum inequality).

easy.q: National Food Security Act was passed in:
easy.qt: தேசிய உணவுப் பாதுகாப்பு சட்டம் இயற்றப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
easy.exp: NFSA (2013) provides legal entitlement to subsidised food grains to ~67% of India's population.

easy.q: Human Development Index (HDI) is published by:
easy.exp: HDI published by UNDP in its annual Human Development Report. Measures life expectancy, education, income.

easy.q: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) was enacted in:
easy.exp: IBC enacted in 2016 to create unified insolvency resolution process for corporates and individuals.

medium.q:
Finance Commission:
1. Not permanent.
2. Art 280, every 5 years.
3. Recommends states' share in central taxes.
medium.qt:
நிதி ஆணையம்:
1. நிரந்தர அமைப்பு அல்ல.
2. Art 280, 5 ஆண்டுதோறும்.
3. மாநில வரிப்பங்கு.
medium.exp: All three correct.
RBI does not regulate insurance — that's IRDAI.
Recommended banking reforms — reduce SLR/CRR, set up Asset Reconstruction Companies.
LPG = Liberalisation + Privatisation + Globalisation — initiated by FM Manmohan Singh.

medium.q: India switched from WPI to CPI as key inflation indicator because:
medium.qt: இந்தியா WPI இலிருந்து CPI க்கு மாறிய காரணம்?
opts: CPI better reflects consumer experience; international practice
medium.exp: RBI switched to CPI (2014 Urjit Patel Committee) — better reflects consumer inflation, aligns with international practice.

opts: High government borrowing raising interest rates, reducing private investment
medium.exp: High government borrowing → higher interest rates → more expensive private borrowing → reduced private investment.

medium.q: NITI Aayog differs from Planning Commission in that:
opts: NITI Aayog is advisory; states are equal partners
medium.exp: NITI Aayog is a policy think-tank; cannot allocate funds (that's Finance Commission). States are equal partners.

opts: Tax rates vs tax revenue — beyond optimal rate revenue falls
medium.exp: Laffer Curve: beyond an optimal tax rate, higher rates yield lower revenue.

opts: Reduce fiscal deficit and debt to sustainable levels
medium.exp: FRBM Act (2003) targets fiscal consolidation — reduce fiscal deficit, eliminate revenue deficit.

medium.q: Balance of Payments — Current Account includes:
medium.exp: Current Account: trade in goods (visible) + services (invisible) + remittances + transfers. FDI is in Capital Account.

opts: Growth benefiting all sections, especially marginalised
medium.exp: Inclusive Growth focuses on reducing inequality and ensuring broad-based benefits for all, especially the poor.

medium.q: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana aims to:
medium.exp: PMAY (2015) — affordable housing for all eligible families, Housing for All mission.

medium.q: 'Base Erosion and Profit Shifting' (BEPS) is about:
medium.exp: BEPS = tax strategies by MNCs to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions. OECD/G20 project addresses this.

medium.qt: அடல் ஓய்வூதிய திட்டம் யாரை இலக்காக கொண்டது?
medium.exp: APY (2015) targets unorganised sector workers 18-40, providing ₹1,000-5,000/month pension after age 60.

opts: ₹6,000 per year income support to small and marginal farmers
medium.exp: PM-Kisan (2019) provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000 each to small and marginal farmers owning up to 2 hectares.

medium.q: The 'Startup India' initiative was launched in:
medium.exp: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016 to build a strong startup ecosystem and promote entrepreneurship in India.

medium.q: 'Small Finance Banks' in India are meant for:
medium.qt: 'சிறு நிதி வங்கிகள்' (Small Finance Banks) இந்தியாவில் எதற்காக?
opts: Basic banking services to underserved sections — small farmers, micro industries, unorganised sector
medium.exp: Small Finance Banks (licensed by RBI) aim to provide basic banking services to underserved and unbanked sections — small farmers, micro industries, unorganised sector workers.

medium.q: India's external sector — which statement is correct?
medium.qt: இந்தியாவின் வெளிப்புற துறை பற்றி சரியான கூற்று?
opts: India always has a trade surplus
India typically has a trade deficit but positive current account due to services and remittances
medium.exp: India typically has a merchandise trade deficit (imports > exports) but partially offset by service exports (IT) and remittances, resulting in a manageable current account deficit.
MSME = Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. They contribute about 30% of India's GDP and 48% of exports.

medium.q: The 'Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code' (IBC) handles resolution within:
medium.qt: IBC கீழ் திவால் தீர்வு செய்யப்படும் காலம்?
medium.exp: IBC mandates the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) to be completed within 180 days (extendable to 270 days maximum).

medium.q: 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' (Self-Reliant India) initiative was announced in:
medium.exp: Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan was announced by PM Narendra Modi in May 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an ₹20 lakh crore economic stimulus package.

medium.q: India's 'National Infrastructure Pipeline' (NIP) aims for infrastructure investment of approximately:
medium.exp: National Infrastructure Pipeline (2019-25) identified ₹111 lakh crore worth of infrastructure projects across sectors like energy, roads, railways, housing.

opts: Union Finance Minister (Chair) + Finance Ministers of all States/UTs
medium.exp: GST Council consists of the Union Finance Minister (Chairperson) and the Finance Ministers of all 28 states and 8 UTs — a constitutional body under Art 279A.

opts: Ensuring all individuals and businesses have access to affordable financial products and services
Tax collection from all income groups
medium.exp: Financial Inclusion = providing affordable, accessible financial products (savings, credit, insurance, payments) to all — especially the unbanked poor.
Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014 to encourage companies to manufacture in India and boost manufacturing sector from 16% to 25% of GDP.

opts: Property rights documentation for rural households using drone technology
medium.exp: PM SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) provides property rights documentation to rural households using drone survey technology.

opts: Digital infrastructure, digital services, and digital literacy for all citizens
medium.exp: Digital India (2015) focuses on three key areas: Digital Infrastructure as utility for every citizen, Governance and Services on Demand, and Digital Empowerment of citizens.
NPS is regulated by PFRDA (Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority), established under the PFRDA Act 2013.

medium.q: India's foreign exchange reserves are held mainly in:
medium.qt: இந்தியாவின் அந்நியச் செலாவணி இருப்பு முக்கியமாக எங்கு வைக்கப்படுகிறது?
opts: RBI manages — in foreign currencies, gold, SDRs, and IMF reserve position
medium.exp: India's forex reserves are managed by RBI and consist of foreign currency assets, gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and reserve tranche position at IMF.
PM Gati Shakti (2021) is a National Master Plan for Multi-modal Connectivity — integrating infrastructure projects across 16 ministries for holistic planning.

opts: Financial incentives to manufacturers based on incremental sales from domestic manufacturing
medium.exp: PLI scheme provides financial incentives (4-6% on incremental sales) to domestic manufacturers to boost domestic manufacturing across 14 sectors including electronics, pharma, autos.

medium.q: 'Green Hydrogen Mission' of India aims to produce green hydrogen using:
opts: Electrolysis of water using renewable energy
medium.exp: Green Hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water using renewable energy (solar/wind), generating zero-carbon hydrogen — India's National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 MMTPA by 2030.

opts: India's currency value relative to a basket of trading partner currencies, adjusted for inflation
medium.exp: REER measures a country's currency value against a weighted basket of trading partners' currencies, adjusted for relative inflation — indicating international competitiveness.

opts: Rural poor and women entrepreneurs who lack access to formal banking
medium.exp: MFIs provide small loans (microfinance) to rural poor, women entrepreneurs, and low-income groups who cannot access formal banking — for income-generating activities.

medium.q: 'Consolidated Fund of India' vs 'Contingency Fund' — key difference?
opts: Consolidated Fund needs Parliament approval for spending; Contingency Fund (Art 267) is for urgent unforeseen expenditure at President's disposal
medium.exp: Consolidated Fund (Art 266) needs Parliamentary approval (Appropriation Act) for withdrawal. Contingency Fund (Art 267, ₹500 crore) is kept at the President's disposal for urgent/unforeseen expenditure — later replenished by Parliament.

medium.q: 'P-Notes' (Participatory Notes) in Indian capital markets are issued by:
medium.qt: இந்திய மூலதன சந்தையில் 'P-நோட்டுகள்' (Participatory Notes) யாரால் வழங்கப்படுகின்றன?
opts: FIIs/FPIs registered with SEBI to overseas investors who want to invest in India without registering with SEBI
Indian companies directly to foreign investors
medium.exp: P-Notes (Offshore Derivative Instruments) are issued by SEBI-registered FIIs/FPIs to overseas investors who want exposure to Indian securities without directly registering with SEBI.

hard.q: Stagflation refers to:
hard.exp: Stagflation = stagnant growth + high inflation + high unemployment. Defies the Phillips Curve.

hard.q: 'Open Market Operations' (OMO) involves:
opts: RBI buying/selling govt securities to control money supply
hard.exp: OMO: RBI buys securities → injects liquidity; sells securities → absorbs liquidity.

hard.q: 'Impossible Trinity' (Mundell-Fleming) states a country cannot simultaneously have:
opts: Low inflation, high growth, full employment
Free capital flow, fixed exchange rate, independent monetary policy
High GDP, low debt, full employment
hard.exp: A country cannot simultaneously maintain free capital movement + fixed exchange rate + independent monetary policy.

hard.q: 'Yield Curve Inversion' typically signals:
hard.qt: 'வட்டி விகிதம் வளைவு மாறுதல்' பொதுவாக என்ன அறிவிக்கிறது?
hard.exp: Yield curve inversion (short-term rates > long-term rates) historically precedes economic recessions.

hard.q: 'Environmental Kuznets Curve' describes:
opts: GDP growth vs environmental degradation (inverted U-shape)
hard.exp: As income rises, pollution first increases then decreases — inverted U-shape. Environmental quality improves at higher income levels.

hard.q: 'Helicopter Money' refers to:
opts: Direct money distribution to citizens by central bank without recovery
hard.exp: Helicopter Money = direct distribution of newly printed money to public by central bank to stimulate economy.

hard.q: Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) was related to:
opts: Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low-Income Households
hard.exp: Recommended universal electronic bank accounts and differentiated banks (payments banks, small finance banks).

hard.q: RBI's 'Prompt Corrective Action' (PCA) is triggered by:
opts: High NPA, low capital adequacy, or negative RoA
hard.exp: PCA triggered for banks with high NPA, low CRAR, or negative Return on Assets — restricts activities to restore health.

hard.q: 'Production Possibility Frontier' (PPF) illustrates:
opts: Trade-off between two goods; opportunity cost; efficiency
hard.exp: PPF shows maximum combinations of two goods with given resources — illustrates opportunity cost and efficiency.

easy.q: India's first satellite:
easy.exp: Aryabhata launched 19 April 1975 by Soviet Intercosmos rocket.

easy.q: Chandrayaan-3 landed on Moon in:
easy.exp: Soft-landed near Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023.

easy.q: C.V. Raman won Nobel Prize for:
easy.exp: Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for discovering the Raman Effect.

easy.q: Father of India's Space Programme:
easy.exp: Dr Vikram Sarabhai established ISRO and founded India's space programme.

easy.q: Father of India's Nuclear Programme:
easy.exp: Dr Homi Jehangir Bhabha established TIFR and BARC.

easy.q: Mangalyaan was launched in:
easy.exp: Mangalyaan launched 5 November 2013; entered Mars orbit 24 September 2014.

easy.q: India's first nuclear test codenamed 'Smiling Buddha' was in:
easy.qt: இந்தியாவின் முதல் அணுகுண்டு சோதனை 'ஸ்மைலிங் புத்தா' ஆண்டு?
easy.exp: India's first nuclear test on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran under PM Indira Gandhi.

easy.q: DNA stands for:
easy.exp: DNA = Deoxyribonucleic Acid — hereditary material in humans and most organisms.

easy.q: Speed of light is approximately:
easy.exp: Speed of light in vacuum ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s (300,000 km/s).

easy.q: Aditya-L1 studies the:
easy.exp: Aditya-L1 (Sept 2023) is India's first solar observatory at Lagrange Point L1.

easy.q: SI unit of electric current:
easy.exp: Ampere (A) is the SI unit of electric current.

easy.q: Penicillin was discovered by:
easy.exp: Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin in 1928.

easy.q: First Indian to go to space:
easy.exp: Rakesh Sharma went to space on 3 April 1984 aboard Soviet Soyuz T-11.

easy.q: Ozone layer is found in the:
easy.exp: Ozone layer in stratosphere (15-35 km). Absorbs harmful UV radiation.

easy.q: Which organ produces insulin?
easy.exp: Pancreas produces insulin. Deficiency causes diabetes mellitus.

easy.q: Hardest natural substance:
easy.exp: Diamond (carbon crystal) = 10 on Mohs hardness scale.

easy.q: ISRO stands for:
easy.exp: ISRO = Indian Space Research Organisation, established 15 August 1969, Bengaluru.

easy.q: Human body has how many chromosomes?
easy.exp: Human cells have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

easy.q: Photosynthesis equation outcome:
opts: CO₂ and water → glucose and oxygen using sunlight
easy.exp: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

easy.q: Seismograph measures:
easy.exp: Seismograph detects, measures, and records earthquakes and seismic waves.

easy.q: GPS stands for:
easy.exp: GPS = Global Positioning System, operated by the US government.

easy.q: Vitamin produced by sunlight exposure:
easy.qt: சூரிய ஒளியில் உடல் உற்பத்தி செய்யும் வைட்டமின்?
easy.exp: Vitamin D produced when skin is exposed to UVB radiation — essential for calcium absorption.

easy.q: DRDO was established in:
easy.exp: DRDO established 1 January 1958 under Ministry of Defence.

easy.q: Fire extinguisher uses which gas?
easy.exp: CO₂ displaces oxygen and cools flames — used in fire extinguishers.

easy.q: Artificial Intelligence refers to:
opts: Simulation of human intelligence by computers
easy.exp: AI = simulation of human intelligence processes — learning, reasoning, problem-solving — by computer systems.

medium.q:
ISRO missions — all correct?
1. Mangalyaan = first interplanetary mission.
2. First country to reach Mars orbit on first attempt.
3. Aditya-L1 = first solar observatory.
medium.qt:
1. மங்கள்யான் — முதல் கிரகங்களுக்கிடையேயான திட்டம்.
2. முதல் முயற்சியில் செவ்வாய்.
3. ஆதித்ய-L1 — முதல் சூரிய கண்காணிப்பு.
medium.exp: All three correct.
APJ Kalam led missile development (Agni, Prithvi). Bhabha→Nuclear; Sarabhai→Space; Chandrasekhar→astrophysics Nobel.

medium.q:
Chandrayaan missions correctly matched?
1. Chandrayaan-1 — discovered water on Moon.
2. Chandrayaan-2 — successful soft landing.
3. Chandrayaan-3 — first soft landing near south pole.
medium.qt:
1. சந்திரயான்-1 — நிலாவில் நீர் கண்டுபிடிப்பு.
2. சந்திரயான்-2 — வெற்றிகரமான தரையிறக்கம்.
3. சந்திரயான்-3 — தென்துருவத்தில் முதல் தரையிறக்கம்.
medium.exp: Chandrayaan-1 (2008): water on Moon (✓). Chandrayaan-2 (2019): Vikram crashed — NOT successful (2 wrong). Chandrayaan-3 (2023): first south pole landing (✓).

opts: Instructing cells to make a protein triggering immune response
medium.exp: mRNA instructs body cells to produce a specific protein (e.g., COVID spike protein), triggering immune response.
PSLV uses 4 stages (alternating solid and liquid propulsion). India's most reliable launch vehicle.
Nanotechnology deals with materials at nanoscale (1-100 nm = 10⁻⁹ m).

medium.q: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) was developed by:
medium.exp: UPI developed by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India), launched April 2016.

medium.q: Quantum computers differ from classical computers in that they:
opts: Use qubits that can exist in multiple states simultaneously (superposition)
medium.exp: Qubits exploit superposition and entanglement for exponentially faster computation on specific problems.

opts: Higher data speeds, lower latency, greater connectivity
medium.exp: 5G: up to 20 Gbps speed, <1ms latency, massive device connectivity — enables IoT, autonomous vehicles.

opts: Gene editing — cutting and modifying DNA precisely
medium.exp: CRISPR-Cas9 is a gene-editing tool allowing precise cutting/modification of DNA sequences.

opts: India and surrounding region up to 1500 km
medium.exp: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) covers India and surrounding region up to 1500 km.
Tejas LCA is India's indigenously designed supersonic fighter aircraft by HAL and ADA.
INS Vikrant (commissioned September 2022) is India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier.
INS Arihant — India's first indigenously built nuclear submarine (SSBN), commissioned 2016.
Blockchain = decentralised, distributed digital ledger. Once recorded, data is immutable.

medium.q: India's National AI Strategy (2018) was released by:
medium.exp: NITI Aayog released India's National AI Strategy in 2018 with vision '#AIforAll'.

opts: Physical devices connected to internet sharing data
medium.exp: IoT = network of physical devices (sensors, appliances, vehicles) sharing data over the internet.

opts: Determining complete DNA sequence of an organism
medium.exp: Genome sequencing = determining all nucleotide sequences in an organism's DNA.

opts: Send Indian astronauts to Low Earth Orbit in Indian spacecraft
medium.exp: Gaganyaan aims to send Indian astronauts (Gagannauts) to LEO (400 km) in an indigenous spacecraft.

medium.q: 'Space Debris Mitigation Policy' was adopted by India in:
medium.exp: India adopted its Space Debris Mitigation Policy in 2021 to reduce the creation of new space debris from ISRO missions.

medium.q: 'One Sun One World One Grid' (OSOWOG) initiative proposes:
opts: Global interconnected solar power grid for cross-border clean energy sharing
medium.exp: OSOWOG (proposed by India at COP26) aims to create a global interconnected power grid to share solar energy across countries, reducing dependence on fossil fuels.

medium.q: 'National Quantum Mission' (NQM) of India was approved in:
medium.exp: India's National Quantum Mission (NQM) was approved in April 2023 with an outlay of ₹6,003 crore to develop quantum technology in computing, communications, sensing, and materials.

opts: Adding material layer by layer to create 3D objects
medium.exp: 3D Printing (Additive Manufacturing) creates three-dimensional objects by depositing material layer by layer based on a digital model.
ISRO's Semi-Cryogenic Engine (SCE-200) uses liquid oxygen (LOX) and kerosene — 'semi-cryogenic' as only one propellant is cryogenic.

medium.q: 'GS SAT' series satellites are used for:
medium.exp: GSAT (Geostationary Satellite) series are Indian communication satellites providing telecommunications, DTH television, VSAT, trunking, and other services.

opts: Sequence the genomes of 10,000 representative Indians to understand genetic diversity
medium.exp: Genome India Project (launched 2020) aims to sequence 10,000 genomes from representative Indian population to understand genetic diversity and develop personalised medicine.

medium.q: India's first Semiconductor Manufacturing Plant is being set up in:
medium.qt: இந்தியாவின் முதல் செமிகண்டக்டர் உற்பத்தி தொழிற்சாலை அமைக்கப்படும் மாநிலம்?
medium.exp: India's first semiconductor fab plant (Tata Electronics with PSMC) is being set up in Dholera, Gujarat under the 'India Semiconductor Mission'.

medium.q: 'LVM3' (previously GSLV Mk III) is significant because:
opts: India's heaviest and most powerful launch vehicle, used for Chandrayaan-3 and Gaganyaan
medium.exp: LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3) is ISRO's heaviest and most powerful rocket — payload capacity 10 tonnes to LEO. Used for Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3, and planned for Gaganyaan.

medium.q: 'Reusable Launch Vehicle' (RLV) technology is being developed by ISRO to:
opts: Significantly reduce cost of accessing space by reusing rocket stages
medium.exp: ISRO's RLV-TD (Reusable Launch Vehicle - Technology Demonstrator) program aims to reduce launch costs by 10x through reusable rocket stages, like SpaceX Falcon 9.

opts: Nuclear fusion reactor that replicates the Sun's energy production
medium.exp: 'Artificial Sun' refers to nuclear fusion reactors (like South Korea's KSTAR, or the international ITER project) that replicate the Sun's fusion process — potentially unlimited clean energy.

opts: Artificial induction of rainfall by dispersing silver iodide or dry ice into clouds
medium.exp: Cloud Seeding is a weather modification technique — dispersing substances (silver iodide, dry ice) into clouds to encourage precipitation and induce rainfall.

opts: Number of transistors in an integrated circuit doubles approximately every 2 years
Computer processing speed halves every year
medium.exp: Moore's Law (Gordon Moore, 1965) observed that the number of transistors in a microchip approximately doubles every 2 years, leading to exponential growth in computing power.

opts: Telecom services, internet services, and broadcasting
medium.exp: TRAI regulates telecom services, internet services, and broadcasting in India — setting tariffs, ensuring quality of service, and protecting consumer interests.

medium.q: 'Telemedicine' in India received a major boost through:
opts: Telemedicine Practice Guidelines (2020) and COVID-19 pandemic
medium.exp: Telemedicine Practice Guidelines released by the Ministry of Health (March 2020) and the COVID-19 pandemic dramatically accelerated telemedicine adoption in India.

opts: Integrated approach recognising interconnection between human, animal, and ecosystem health
medium.exp: 'One Health' is an integrated, collaborative approach recognising that human health, animal health, and ecosystem/environmental health are interconnected and interdependent.

opts: AI (deep learning) to create hyper-realistic fake videos/images of people
medium.exp: Deep Fake uses deep learning AI (specifically Generative Adversarial Networks — GANs) to create hyper-realistic fake videos where a person appears to say or do things they never did.
PARAM Siddhi is a high-performance computing (HPC) AI supercomputer built under India's National Supercomputing Mission, ranked among top 100 globally in 2020.

medium.q: 'Comet' differs from an 'Asteroid' mainly in that:
opts: Comets have a coma and tail (due to ices vaporizing); asteroids are rocky/metallic without coma
medium.exp: Comets are composed of ice, dust, and rocky material — when near the Sun, their ices vaporize forming a bright coma and tail. Asteroids are mainly rocky/metallic without ices.

medium.q: 'Dark Energy' constitutes approximately what percentage of the universe?
medium.qt: 'இருண்ட ஆற்றல்' (Dark Energy) பிரபஞ்சத்தில் சுமார் எத்தனை சதவீதம்?
medium.exp: Dark Energy constitutes ~68% of the universe (dark matter ~27%, ordinary matter ~5%). Dark Energy is hypothesised to be causing the universe's accelerating expansion.

opts: Accelerate development of affordable biopharmaceuticals and vaccines in India
