medium.exp: National Biopharma Mission (2017) aims to accelerate biopharmaceutical development — vaccines, biosimilars, diagnostics — building India's domestic biopharmaceutical ecosystem.

medium.q: 'Chandrayaan-1' found water/hydroxyl on the Moon using which instrument?
opts: Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3 by NASA on Chandrayaan-1)
medium.exp: The Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3), a NASA instrument on Chandrayaan-1, discovered water molecules and hydroxyl on the lunar surface in 2009.

medium.q: 'Artificial Intelligence' in healthcare can help with:
opts: Disease diagnosis from images, drug discovery, personalised treatment, and predicting outbreaks
medium.exp: AI in healthcare assists with: medical image analysis (radiology), drug discovery acceleration, personalized treatment plans, disease prediction, and administrative efficiency — supplementing, not replacing, doctors.
PARAM Ananta supercomputer (under National Supercomputing Mission) was installed at IIT Gandhinagar in 2022.

hard.q:
Dark Matter — which are correct?
1. Interacts with electromagnetic force.
2. ~27% of universe's mass-energy.
3. Inferred from gravitational effects.
hard.qt:
1. மின்காந்த விசையுடன் தொடர்பு.
2. ~27% திணிவு-ஆற்றல்.
3. ஈர்ப்பு விளைவால் அனுமானிக்கப்படுகிறது.
hard.exp: Dark Matter does NOT interact with EM force — invisible (1 wrong). ~27% correct. Inferred from gravitational lensing/galaxy rotation (✓).

hard.q:
India's nuclear doctrine — which are correct?
1. No-First-Use (NFU) policy.
2. India has nuclear triad.
3. India joined NPT as nuclear weapons state.
hard.qt:
1. முதலில் பயன்படுத்தாது கொள்கை (NFU).
2. மூன்று வகை தாக்குதல் அமைப்பு.
3. NPT இல் அணுசக்தி நாடாக சேர்ந்தது.
hard.exp: NFU (✓). Nuclear triad: Agni missiles + aircraft + Arihant submarines (✓). India has NOT signed NPT — outside the treaty (3 wrong).

hard.q: Voyager 1 is significant because:
opts: First human-made object in interstellar space
hard.exp: Voyager 1 (1977) entered interstellar space in 2012 — most distant man-made object.

hard.q: Schrödinger's Cat thought experiment illustrates:
opts: Quantum superposition — system in multiple states until observed
hard.exp: Illustrates quantum superposition applied to macroscopic objects — cat both alive and dead until observed.

hard.q: Higgs Boson is important because:
opts: Gives mass to elementary particles via Higgs field
hard.exp: Higgs Boson (discovered CERN 2012) confirms the Higgs field which gives mass to elementary particles. Nobel 2013.

hard.q: 'CRISPR' stands for:
opts: Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats
Circular Replication in Specific Protein Regions
Controlled RNA Interference for Specific Protein Regulation
hard.exp: CRISPR = Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats — naturally occurring sequences in bacteria.

hard.q: 'Fermi Paradox' refers to:
opts: Contradiction between high probability of alien life and lack of evidence
hard.exp: Fermi Paradox: given vast universe and probability of alien life, why haven't we detected any signs of extraterrestrial intelligence?

hard.q: Remote Sensing applications include:
opts: Crop monitoring, disaster management, urban planning, mineral exploration
hard.exp: Remote sensing: crop health, flood/disaster management, urban sprawl, deforestation, mineral exploration.

culture.exp: Originated in Tamil Nadu from devadasi temple tradition. Revived by Rukmini Devi Arundale.
Ajanta (2nd BCE–6th CE) mainly depicts Buddhist Jataka tales.
Mohiniyattam = classical dance of Kerala, graceful swaying movements.
Bharata Muni (200 BCE–200 CE) — foundational treatise on Indian performing arts.
Konark Sun Temple in Odisha — UNESCO WHS, built by Narasimhadeva I (13th century).

culture.q: Dravidian temple architecture is characterized by:
culture.exp: Dravidian style = tall ornate Gopuram (gateway towers). Nagara style = Shikhara.

culture.q: Carnatic music is practiced primarily in:
culture.exp: Carnatic classical music = TN, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Kerala.
Kuchipudi from Kuchipudi village, AP — fast rhythmic footwork.
Trinity: Thyagaraja (1767–1847), Syama Sastri (1762–1827), Muthuswami Dikshitar (1775–1835).
Odissi = classical dance of Odisha, from temple Mahari and Gotipua dancer traditions.
Rath Yatra = annual chariot festival of Lord Jagannath at Puri, Odisha.

culture.q: Kathak is associated with which region?
culture.exp: Kathak = classical dance of North India (UP), originating from storytelling Kathakas.

culture.q: National anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was composed by:
culture.exp: Jana Gana Mana composed by Rabindranath Tagore. Adopted 24 January 1950.
Lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) is India's national flower.
Manipuri dance — gentle, lyrical, based on Vaishnavite themes.
Kangra Painting (Pahari School) from Himachal Pradesh — delicate brushwork, Krishna's life scenes.
Madhubani (Mithila) painting from Bihar — geometric patterns, Hindu deities.

culture.q: Hampi ruins are remains of the:
culture.exp: Hampi (UNESCO) was capital of the Vijayanagara Empire (14th–17th century) in Karnataka.
Tansen = Akbar's greatest court musician, one of the Nine Gems (Navaratnas).
Sangam literature: ancient Tamil corpus compiled in three Sangam periods, ~300 BCE–300 CE.

culture.q: Ajanta and Ellora Caves are in:
culture.exp: Both in Aurangabad, Maharashtra — both UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Khajuraho (UNESCO, Madhya Pradesh) — intricate sculptural work and excellent Nagara architecture.
Tamil is one of the world's oldest living classical languages with 2,000+ years of literature.
Pongal is Tamil Nadu's harvest festival, celebrated in mid-January.
Warli tribal art from Maharashtra — geometric shapes depicting daily life.
Qutb ud-Din Aibak started (1193) and Iltutmish completed (1220) the Qutub Minar.

culture.q: Bihu is a folk dance/festival from:
culture.exp: Bihu = national folk dance and harvest festival of Assam (three types: Bohag, Kati, Magh).
Bhangra = energetic folk dance of Punjab, associated with Baisakhi harvest festival.
Diwali celebrates Lord Ram's return to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and victory over Ravana.

opts: Melodic frameworks with ascending/descending note patterns
culture.exp: A Raga = melodic framework (notes, rules for ascent/descent, characteristic phrases) conveying a specific mood.
Ellora: 17 Hindu + 12 Buddhist + 5 Jain caves — unique religious harmony.
4 Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda.
Thiruvalluvar wrote Thirukkural — 1330 couplets on Aram, Porul, Inbam.
Pattachitra (scroll painting) practiced in Odisha and West Bengal — Jagannath mythology.

culture.q: Ganesh Chaturthi most prominently celebrated in:
culture.exp: Maharashtra (especially Mumbai and Pune). Popularised by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
Lohri celebrated in Punjab/Haryana on 13 January — end of winter, harvest.
Sattriya = classical dance from Assam, founded by 15th-century saint Srimanta Sankardev.

culture.q: City of Temples in Tamil Nadu:
culture.exp: Madurai = Temple City, famous for the Meenakshi Amman Temple.
Garba = circular folk dance from Gujarat, performed during Navratri in honour of Goddess Durga.
Shore Temples and rock-cut monuments built by Pallava kings (7th–8th century CE), especially Narasimhavarman I.

culture.q: Guru Granth Sahib is the scripture of:
culture.qt: 'குரு கிரந்த சாஹிப்' எந்த மதத்தின் புனித நூல்?
culture.exp: Guru Granth Sahib is the eternal living Guru and scripture of Sikhism.
Andal (Kodhai) — only female Alvar — composed Thirupaavai (30 verses), sung during Margazhi.
Pashmina comes from the Changthangi goat of Ladakh/Kashmir Changthang plateau — one of the finest fibres.
Pushkar Camel Fair held annually in Pushkar, Rajasthan — one of the world's largest camel fairs.

culture.q: Sitar is which type of instrument?
culture.exp: Sitar = plucked string instrument. Ravi Shankar brought it to global recognition.
Original Ramayana composed in Sanskrit by Valmiki (24,000 slokas). Tamil version by Kambar (12th century).

culture.q: UNESCO Intangible Heritage from India includes:
culture.qt: இந்தியாவிலிருந்து UNESCO அருமதியான கலாச்சார பாரம்பரியப் பட்டியல்?
opts: Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Chhau dance, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja, Garba and others
culture.exp: UNESCO ICH from India includes: Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Chhau, Kalbelia, Mudiyettu, Thatheras, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Kolkata Durga Puja, Garba.
Gita Govinda by Jayadeva (12th century) — lyrical Sanskrit poem about Radha-Krishna.
4 Vedas: Rigveda (oldest), Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda.

culture.q: Mahabharata is called the '5th Veda' because:
opts: It made spiritual knowledge accessible to those who couldn't study the four Vedas
It is the largest Sanskrit text
It was composed 5 centuries after the Vedas
culture.exp: Mahabharata (attributed to Vyasa) = 'Fifth Veda' as it brought Vedic wisdom to common people who couldn't study the original four Vedas.

opts: Buddhist themes in natural mineral colours, intricate narrative art
culture.exp: Ajanta (2nd BCE–6th CE) — Buddhist themes painted in natural mineral colours, showing sophisticated artistic techniques.

opts: Elaborate costumes with large headgear, and stylized face paint depicting character types
culture.exp: Kathakali (Kerala) is known for elaborate costumes, large headgear (Kireedam), and detailed face paint that identifies character types (Pacha, Kathi, Minukku etc.).

culture.q: Nayanmars are associated with which religion?
culture.exp: The 63 Nayanmars are Tamil Shaivite saints (devotees of Lord Shiva), part of the Tamil Bhakti movement.

culture.q: The 'Deccan Sultanates' emerged from the break-up of:
culture.exp: Five Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar) emerged from break-up of the Bahmani Sultanate in 1518.
Sangeet Natak Akademi — national academy for music, dance, and drama — established 31 May 1952.
Dilwara Temples near Mount Abu, Rajasthan are exquisite Jain marble temples (11th-13th century CE), famous for intricate white marble carvings.

culture.q: 'Chaturanga' is the ancient Indian game that evolved into:
culture.qt: 'சதுரங்க' என்ற பண்டைய இந்திய விளையாட்டு எதாக வளர்ந்தது?
culture.exp: Chaturanga (Sanskrit: 'four divisions of the military') is the ancient Indian game from which modern Chess evolved, via Persian Shatranj.

culture.q: 'ICCR' (Indian Council for Cultural Relations) was founded by:
culture.exp: ICCR established in 1950 by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (India's first Education Minister) to promote India's culture internationally.

culture.q: Tansen Music Festival is held at:
culture.exp: Tansen Music Festival held annually at Gwalior, MP, near Tansen's tomb.
Chhau practiced in three states: Seraikella (Jharkhand), Mayurbhanj (Odisha), Purulia (West Bengal). UNESCO 2010.

culture.q: Sangam age literature is classified into Akam and Puram representing:
culture.qt: சங்க கால இலக்கியம் அகம் மற்றும் புறம் என பிரிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது — அவை குறிக்கும் கருத்து?
culture.exp: Akam = subjective love poetry; Puram = objective heroic/public poetry about war, valor, kings' generosity.
Kathakali = classical dance-drama of Kerala — elaborate costumes, makeup, expressing Hindu epics.
Kolam (called Rangoli in North, Muggu in Andhra) predominantly practiced in Tamil Nadu — geometric rice-flour patterns.

culture.q: Brihadeeshwarar temple at Thanjavur was built by:
culture.exp: Rajaraja Chola I (985–1014 CE) built the Brihadeeshwarar Temple — UNESCO WHS, largest Dravidian temple.

culture.q: Hinayana and Mahayana are schools of:
culture.exp: Hinayana (Theravada) and Mahayana are two main schools of Buddhism.

culture.q: Bodhisattva concept in Buddhism refers to:
opts: Being who delays nirvana to help all sentient beings
culture.exp: Bodhisattva = enlightened being who delays own Nirvana to help all beings achieve liberation. Central to Mahayana.

culture.q: Upanishads are part of which literature?
culture.exp: Upanishads (108 in number) are the philosophical concluding portion of the Vedas (Vedanta). 800-500 BCE.

opts: Distinguished service of high order in any field
culture.exp: Padma Awards (Vibhushan, Bhushan, Shri) for distinguished service in any field — art, science, public affairs, etc.
Ancient Silk Road connected India with Central Asia, Persia (Iran), and China, facilitating trade and cultural exchange.

culture.q: The 'Kolkata Durga Puja' was inscribed by UNESCO on ICH list in:
culture.qt: கொல்கத்தா துர்கா பூஜை யுனெஸ்கோ பட்டியலில் சேர்க்கப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
culture.exp: Durga Puja of Kolkata was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list in December 2021.

culture.q: Garba dance was inscribed on UNESCO ICH list in:
culture.qt: கர்பா நடனம் யுனெஸ்கோ பட்டியலில் சேர்க்கப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
culture.exp: Garba of Gujarat was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in December 2023.

culture.q: Meenakshi Amman Temple is famous for:
culture.exp: Madurai Meenakshi Amman Temple — 12 towering gopurams, thousands of intricate sculptures.
Brihadaranyaka Upanishad is associated with the Shukla Yajurveda — one of the oldest, most important Upanishads.
Nagarjunasagar Dam across Krishna River in Telangana/AP — one of world's largest masonry dams.

culture.q: 'Chaturanga' → Chess — the ancient game originated in:
culture.exp: Chess originated in India as Chaturanga (~6th century CE), spread to Persia as Shatranj, then to the West as Chess.

culture.q: 'Yakshagana' is a traditional theatre form from:
culture.exp: Yakshagana is a traditional theatre form from Karnataka combining dance, music, dialogue, and costume based on mythological themes.
Hornbill Festival is celebrated in Nagaland every December — a cultural extravaganza showcasing the traditions of all Naga tribes.

culture.q: 'Theyyam' is a ritual dance form from:
culture.exp: Theyyam is a ritual dance form from the Malabar region of northern Kerala — a form of worship where the performer becomes the deity.
Chikankari is a traditional embroidery style from Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh) — delicate hand embroidery with floral motifs on fine fabric.

culture.q: The 'Dashavatar' cycle in Indian art represents:
culture.exp: Dashavatar refers to the 10 principal avatars (incarnations) of Lord Vishnu — Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Krishna (or Balarama), Buddha, and Kalki.

opts: An ancient Indian martial art from Kerala
culture.exp: Kalaripayattu is an ancient Indian martial art originating from Kerala, considered one of the oldest fighting systems in the world — includes strikes, kicks, grappling, and weapons.

culture.q: The 'Vedanta' school of philosophy is associated with:
opts: Study of the Vedas' concluding portions (Upanishads) and metaphysical concepts
culture.exp: Vedanta ('end of the Vedas') is based on the Upanishads, Brahma Sutras, and Bhagavad Gita. Major sub-schools: Advaita (Shankaracharya), Vishishtadvaita (Ramanuja), Dvaita (Madhvacharya).
Lavani is a traditional folk dance of Maharashtra performed to dhol beats.
Kambala is a traditional buffalo race held in the Tulu Nadu region of coastal Karnataka, especially in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts.
Ghumar is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan performed by Bhil tribe women, characterized by graceful swirling movements. Now considered the 'folk dance of Rajasthan'.

opts: A battle formation shaped like a lotus
culture.exp: Padmavyuha (Chakravyuha) in the Mahabharata was a military formation shaped like a lotus/spiral — Abhimanyu (Arjuna's son) entered it but couldn't exit, leading to his death.

opts: Nayanmars' (Shaivite saints') Tamil hymns compiled in 12 volumes
culture.exp: Thirumurai is a 12-volume collection of Tamil hymns by the 63 Nayanmars (Shaivite saints). The first 11 volumes include works by saints like Appar, Sundarar, Thirugnanasambandar. The 12th (Periya Puranam) is by Sekkizhar.

mixed.exp: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with Chanakya's guidance.

mixed.q: In which year did India gain independence?
mixed.exp: India gained independence on 15 August 1947.
Jawaharlal Nehru wrote it in Ahmednagar jail in 1944.

mixed.q: Ashoka embraced Buddhism after which battle?
mixed.qt: அசோகர் எந்த போருக்கு பின் பௌத்தம் ஏற்றார்?
mixed.exp: The Kalinga War (261 BCE) devastated Ashoka, leading him to embrace Buddhism.

mixed.q: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
mixed.exp: Shah Jahan built it as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal, completed ~1648 CE.

mixed.q: Who launched the Quit India Movement in 1942?
mixed.exp: Gandhi launched it on 8 August 1942 at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Mumbai.

mixed.q: The Battle of Plassey was fought in:
mixed.exp: Fought 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company and Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah.

mixed.q: The first President of India was:
mixed.exp: Dr Rajendra Prasad served as first President from 1950 to 1962.

mixed.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
mixed.exp: INC was founded on 28 December 1885 by A.O. Hume in Bombay.

mixed.q: The first Battle of Panipat was fought in:
mixed.exp: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526, establishing the Mughal Empire.

mixed.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
mixed.exp: General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful crowd on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar.
Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

mixed.q: The Dandi March took place in:
mixed.exp: Gandhi's Salt March began 12 March 1930 and ended 6 April 1930, covering 241 miles.

mixed.q: Who gave the slogan 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom'?
mixed.qt: 'என் இரத்தம் தாருங்கள், சுதந்திரம் தருகிறேன்' என்று கூறியவர்?
mixed.exp: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose gave this slogan to motivate Indians to join the INA.

mixed.q: The partition of India and Pakistan occurred in:
mixed.exp: Partition based on the Mountbatten Plan took place on 14-15 August 1947.

mixed.q: Tipu Sultan was the ruler of:
mixed.exp: Tipu Sultan (Tiger of Mysore) ruled Mysore and died fighting the British in 1799.

mixed.q: Simon Commission came to India in:
mixed.exp: Simon Commission arrived February 1928 and was boycotted as it had no Indian members.

mixed.q: The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 began at:
mixed.exp: The Revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857 over the greased cartridges issue.

mixed.q: Who gave the title 'Mahatma' to Gandhi?
mixed.exp: Rabindranath Tagore gave the title 'Mahatma' (Great Soul) to Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi.

mixed.q: Who was the founder of the Sikh religion?
mixed.exp: Guru Nanak (1469–1539) founded Sikhism and was the first of ten Sikh Gurus.

mixed.q: The Indus Valley Civilization flourished approximately:
mixed.exp: The civilization peaked around 2500-2000 BCE in the Indus River valley.
Lala Lajpat Rai died from police lathi blows during protests against the Simon Commission in 1928.

mixed.q: The Battle of Buxar was fought in:
mixed.exp: Battle of Buxar (1764) was a decisive British victory consolidating power in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
Harihara I and Bukka Raya I founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE near Hampi.
Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Samaj in 1828, campaigning against sati and child marriage.
Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.

mixed.q: The Rowlatt Act was passed in:
mixed.exp: Rowlatt Act (1919) allowed imprisonment without trial, sparking massive protests by Gandhi.

mixed.q: Who was the last Mughal Emperor?
mixed.exp: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal Emperor, exiled to Rangoon after the 1857 Revolt.

mixed.q: The Chola dynasty was famous for its:
mixed.exp: Chola dynasty (9th–13th c.) was famous for magnificent bronze sculptures (Nataraja) and naval power.

mixed.q: The first Governor-General of India was:
mixed.exp: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773.

mixed.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
mixed.exp: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister, serving from 1947 until his death in 1964.
The Poona Pact was signed between Gandhi (who was on hunger strike) and B.R. Ambedkar regarding separate electorates for depressed classes.

mixed.q: Who is called the 'Iron Man of India'?
mixed.exp: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is called the 'Iron Man of India' for unifying the 562 princely states into the Indian Union.

mixed.q: Vasco da Gama first arrived in India in:
mixed.exp: Vasco da Gama first arrived at Kozhikode (Calicut), Kerala on 20 May 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India.

mixed.q: The 'Cabinet Mission' came to India in:
mixed.exp: The Cabinet Mission (1946) proposed a united India with federal structure, but it was eventually rejected.

mixed.q: The Revolt of 1857 is also called:
mixed.exp: V.D. Savarkar called the Revolt of 1857 the 'First War of Indian Independence'. The British called it 'Sepoy Mutiny'.

mixed.q: Who designed the Indian National Flag?
mixed.exp: Pingali Venkaiah designed the Indian National Flag. The final version was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947.

mixed.q: The 'Servants of India Society' was founded by:
mixed.exp: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 to train workers for national service.

mixed.q:
Which of the following about the Indus Valley Civilization is/are correct?
1. Worshipped male and female deities.
2. Used horse-drawn chariots in warfare.
3. Cotton used for textiles.
mixed.qt:
சிந்து வெளி நாகரிகம்:
1. ஆண், பெண் தெய்வங்கள் வழிபட்டனர்.
2. குதிரை ரதங்கள் பயன்படுத்தினர்.
3. பருத்தி நெசவுக்கு பயன்பட்டது.
mixed.exp: Worshipped both (✓). Cotton textiles (✓). No evidence of horse chariots in Indus civilization (✗).
Lord Wellesley introduced Subsidiary Alliance in 1798, forcing Indian rulers to accept British troops.

mixed.q: Who among these was NOT a Bhakti movement saint?
mixed.exp: Shankaracharya (8th c.) propagated Advaita Vedanta — he predated the Bhakti movement.

mixed.q: The Ghadar Party was founded in:
mixed.qt: கதர் கட்சி நிறுவப்பட்ட இடம் மற்றும் ஆண்டு?
mixed.exp: Ghadar Party was founded in San Francisco in 1913 by Lala Har Dayal.

mixed.q: Correct chronological order: 1-Plassey  2-1857 Revolt  3-INC formation  4-Partition of Bengal
mixed.exp: Plassey 1757 → Revolt 1857 → INC 1885 → Partition of Bengal 1905.
Rajendra Chola I (1014–1044 CE) conquered Ceylon and expanded the empire to Southeast Asia.

opts: A new syncretic religion he founded
mixed.exp: Din-i-Ilahi (1582) was a syncretic religion combining Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, and Christianity.

mixed.q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between:
mixed.exp: The Marathas were decisively defeated by Ahmad Shah Durrani (Abdali) in 1761.

mixed.q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was used by:
mixed.exp: Lord Dalhousie (1848–56) used Doctrine of Lapse to annex Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, and others.
Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in 1875, promoting Vedic learning and opposing idol worship.

mixed.q: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India was at:
mixed.exp: Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar protested against the forced indigo cultivation system.

mixed.q: The Permanent Settlement (1793) was introduced by:
mixed.exp: Lord Cornwallis introduced Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System) in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa.

mixed.q: The Khilafat Movement was launched to support:
mixed.exp: Khilafat Movement (1919–24) by Ali Brothers supported the Ottoman Caliphate against British policies.

mixed.q: The Home Rule League was founded by:
mixed.exp: Two Home Rule Leagues were founded in 1916 — Tilak's in Pune, Annie Besant's in Madras.

mixed.q: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
mixed.exp: Dadabhai Naoroji (1825–1917) was the first Indian elected to British Parliament and propounded the 'Drain Theory'.

mixed.q: Which Gupta ruler is called the 'Napoleon of India'?
mixed.exp: Samudragupta (335–375 CE) is called the 'Napoleon of India' by historian V.A. Smith.

mixed.q: Cripps Mission came to India in:
mixed.exp: Cripps Mission (March 1942) proposed dominion status after WWII — rejected by both INC and Muslim League.

mixed.q: Who established the Indian National Army (INA)?
mixed.exp: Subhas Chandra Bose reorganized and led the INA (Azad Hind Fauj) from 1943 with Japanese support.
Lucknow Pact (1916) was signed between INC and All India Muslim League for joint action against the British.
Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims — a key step toward communal politics.
Lord William Bentinck abolished Sati by Regulation XVII in 1829, following Ram Mohan Roy's campaign.
Dadabhai Naoroji showed in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) how British rule drained India's wealth.

mixed.q: The Vernacular Press Act was passed by:
mixed.exp: Lord Lytton passed the Vernacular Press Act in 1878 to muzzle Indian-language press. Repealed by Ripon in 1882.
Muhammad Ali Jinnah propounded the two-nation theory — Hindus and Muslims as separate nations — leading to partition.

mixed.q: The Battle of Talikota (1565) resulted in:
mixed.exp: Deccan Sultanate coalition defeated Vijayanagara; capital Hampi was destroyed and the empire rapidly declined.

mixed.q: Who wrote 'Indica', the Greek account of Mauryan India?
mixed.qt: மௌரிய இந்தியாவை பற்றிய கிரேக்க நூல் 'இண்டிகா' ஆசிரியர்?
mixed.exp: Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador at Chandragupta Maurya's court and authored 'Indica'.

mixed.q:
The Bhakti Movement in Tamil Nadu — which are correct?
1. Nayanmars were Shaivite devotees.
2. Alvars were Vaishnava devotees.
3. Their verses form Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
mixed.qt:
1. நாயன்மார்கள் சைவர்கள்.
2. ஆழ்வார்கள் வைஷ்ணவர்கள்.
3. நாலாயிர திவ்ய பிரபந்தம்.
mixed.exp: All correct. 63 Nayanmars (Shiva), 12 Alvars (Vishnu), 4000 verses of Alvars = Nalayira Divya Prabandham.

mixed.q: Gandhiji's Champaran Movement (1917) was related to:
mixed.exp: Champaran Satyagraha protested the forced indigo cultivation (tinkathia system) imposed by British planters.

mixed.q: The 'Ryotwari Settlement' was a direct settlement between:
mixed.exp: Ryotwari (introduced by Thomas Munro in Madras) was a direct settlement between the colonial government and individual peasants.

mixed.q: The Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) was primarily caused by:
opts: Zamindari exploitation and British land laws
mixed.exp: The Santhal Rebellion was caused by exploitation by zamindars, moneylenders, and unjust British land settlement displacing tribals.

mixed.q: The 'Mahad Satyagraha' (1927) was led by B.R. Ambedkar to assert the right of:
opts: Dalit access to a public tank (water source)
mixed.exp: Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha in 1927 to assert the right of untouchables to draw water from the Chowdar Tank in Mahad, Maharashtra.

mixed.q: The 'Divide and Rule' policy in India refers to:
opts: British strategy of creating divisions between communities to maintain control
mixed.exp: 'Divide and Rule' was the British colonial strategy of deliberately creating and exploiting communal, caste, and regional divisions to prevent unified opposition.

mixed.q:
Arrange these reform movements chronologically:
1. Brahmo Samaj  2. Arya Samaj  3. Ramakrishna Mission  4. Theosophical Society
mixed.qt: காலவரிசைப்படி: 1. பிரம்ம சமாஜ் 2. ஆர்ய சமாஜ் 3. ராமகிருஷ்ண மிஷன் 4. தியோசாஃபிகல் சொசைட்டி
mixed.exp: Brahmo Samaj (1828) → Arya Samaj (1875) → Theosophical Society in India (1882) → Ramakrishna Mission (1897).
Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced Dyarchy — some subjects transferred to elected Indian ministers, others reserved for the Governor.

Gandhi's Eleven Vows included Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Brahmacharya (celibacy), Asteya (non-stealing), Aparigraha (non-possession), Sharirshrama (bread labour), Aswada, Sarvatra Bhayavarjana, Sarva Dharma Samanatva, Swadeshi, Sparshbhavana.

mixed.q: The 'Vande Mataram' song is from which literary work?
mixed.exp: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankimchandra Chatterjee in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882). First sung at INC session in 1896.
Swadeshi Movement (1905-08) was triggered by the partition of Bengal. Indians boycotted British goods and promoted Indian-made products.

mixed.q: The 'Lucknow Session of INC' (1916) was significant because:
opts: Lucknow Pact between INC and Muslim League was signed
mixed.exp: The 1916 Lucknow Session was significant because of the Lucknow Pact between INC and Muslim League, and Tilak's return to INC.

mixed.q: Who was the Viceroy when India gained independence?
mixed.exp: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India (1947). He oversaw the partition and independence of India and Pakistan.

mixed.q: The 'Quit India Resolution' was passed at:
mixed.exp: The Quit India Resolution was passed at the AICC session in Bombay (Mumbai) on 8 August 1942.

mixed.q: The 'Indian Independence Act 1947' was passed by the British Parliament on:
mixed.qt: 'இந்திய சுதந்திர சட்டம் 1947' பிரிட்டிஷ் நாடாளுமன்றத்தில் நிறைவேற்றப்பட்ட தேதி?
mixed.exp: The Indian Independence Act 1947 was passed by British Parliament on 18 July 1947. It provided for the creation of two independent dominions — India and Pakistan — from 15 August 1947.

mixed.q: Who was the first woman President of Indian National Congress?
mixed.qt: இந்திய தேசிய காங்கிரஸின் முதல் பெண் தலைவர்?
mixed.exp: Annie Besant became the first woman President of INC in 1917.

opts: Separate electorates for Harijans as originally proposed
Reserved seats in general (joint) electorates instead of separate electorates for depressed classes
mixed.exp: Poona Pact replaced the Communal Award's separate electorates for depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates, preventing communal division of Hindu society.

opts: British trade restrictions and revenue policies in Bengal
mixed.exp: The Sanyasi Rebellion in Bengal (1763-1800) was by wandering Hindu monks (sanyasis) and fakirs against British trade restrictions and revenue policies that caused food shortages.

opts: Bring the East India Company under Parliamentary control
mixed.exp: Regulating Act 1773 was Britain's first step to regulate the East India Company — creating the post of Governor-General and a Supreme Court.
Gandhi wrote 'Hind Swaraj' (Indian Home Rule) in 1909, articulating his vision of Indian self-rule based on moral regeneration.
The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected its President on 11 December 1946.
Kheda Satyagraha (1918) demanded revenue exemption for Gujarat farmers hit by crop failure and plague. Gandhi's support established his national stature.

opts: Tolerance, non-violence, moral conduct, respect for all religions
mixed.exp: Ashoka's Dhamma was a moral code emphasizing tolerance, non-violence, respect for all sects, care for humans and animals, and righteous conduct — not Buddhist dogma per se.

mixed.q: The 'Bengal Famine' of 1943 was primarily caused by:
opts: War-time policies, hoarding, and Bengal's rice exports to military — deliberate policy failure
mixed.exp: The Bengal Famine (1943) killed 2-3 million people — caused by WWII war-time policies (rice denial to prevent Japanese use), exports, speculation, and hoarding. Churchill's policies are considered a major cause.

mixed.q: 'Ashoka Stambha' (Pillar Edict) at Sarnath is the source of India's:
mixed.exp: India's National Emblem is derived from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath — adopted on 26 January 1950. It shows four lions on an Abacus with a Dharma Chakra.

opts: Established by British; Indians were barred until 1864; Satyendranath Tagore was first Indian to pass
mixed.exp: ICS was established by the British. The covenanted civil service was initially closed to Indians. Satyendranath Tagore (Rabindranath Tagore's brother) was the first Indian to pass the ICS exam in 1864.

mixed.q: To convert a Saka Era year to CE, add:
mixed.qt: சக சகாப்தத்திலிருந்து கி.பி.ஆக மாற்ற எத்தனை ஆண்டுகள் கூட்ட வேண்டும்?
mixed.exp: Saka Era began 78 CE. Add 78 to convert. Important for reading ancient inscriptions.
All correct. Kalhana (Kashmir history), Barani (Firuz Shah's reign), Abu'l-Fazl (Akbar's admin account).

mixed.q:
Charvaka philosophy — which are correct?
1. Accepted Vedas as authority.
2. Pleasure is ultimate goal.
3. Rejected soul's existence.
mixed.qt:
1. வேதங்களை ஆதாரமாக ஏற்றது.
2. இன்பம் வாழ்வின் இலக்கு.
3. ஆன்மாவின் இருப்பை மறுத்தது.
mixed.exp: Charvaka REJECTED Vedas (1 wrong). Believed in pleasure as goal (✓). Denied eternal soul (✓).

mixed.q:
Mansabdari system — which is correct?
1. Mansab denoted military rank and civil status.
2. Zat rank = cavalry to maintain.
3. Sawar rank = personal rank.
mixed.qt:
1. மன்சப் இராணுவ மற்றும் சிவில் தரத்தை குறித்தது.
2. ஜாட் = குதிரைவீரர் எண்ணிக்கை.
3. சவார் = தனிப்பட்ட தரம்.
mixed.exp: Zat = personal rank; Sawar = cavalry rank. Statements 2 and 3 are reversed. Only Statement 1 is correct.

mixed.q: 'Home Charges' in British India referred to:
opts: India's payments to Britain for civil/military expenses
mixed.exp: Home Charges = annual payments by India to Britain for admin, military costs, debt interest — key part of Drain of Wealth.

mixed.q: The Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) is significant because:
opts: Exposed racial discrimination; mobilised Indian opinion
mixed.exp: European fierce opposition to Indian judges trying Europeans exposed racism and united Indians — contributing to INC formation in 1885.

mixed.q:
Uprising-Leader pairs:
1. Santhal Rebellion — Sidhu and Kanhu
2. Moplah Rebellion — Mambaram Tangal
3. Indigo Revolt — Bishnucharan Biswas
mixed.exp: Santhal: Sidhu and Kanhu (✓). Indigo: Bishnucharan Biswas (✓). Moplah (1921): Ali Musaliar, not Mambaram Tangal.

mixed.q:
Sufism in medieval India — which are correct?
1. Khanqah = Sufi hospice.
2. Chishti order emphasised poverty, rejected royal patronage.
3. Silsila = spiritual lineage.
mixed.qt:
1. கான்காஹ் = ஆன்மீக மையம்.
2. சிஷ்டி வழிமுறை வறுமையை வலியுறுத்தியது.
3. சில்சிலா = ஆன்மீக வம்சாவழி.
mixed.exp: All three correct. Khanqah (✓). Chishti poverty/no royal patronage (✓). Silsila = chain/lineage (✓).

mixed.q: Arrange: 1-Regulating Act  2-Pitt's India Act  3-Charter Act 1833  4-Govt of India Act 1858
mixed.exp: Regulating Act (1773) → Pitt's India Act (1784) → Charter Act (1833) → Govt of India Act (1858).

mixed.q: Which of these was NOT part of Gandhi's 'Constructive Programme'?
mixed.exp: Boycott was part of Non-Cooperation/Swadeshi — not Constructive Programme. CP included Khadi, sanitation, unity, women's uplift.

mixed.q:
The 'Devadasi system' — which is/are correct?
1. Prevalent only in South India.
2. Associated with temple worship.
3. British first legislated against it.
mixed.qt:
1. தென்னிந்தியாவில் மட்டும்.
2. கோயில் வழிபாட்டுடன் தொடர்புடையது.
3. பிரிட்டிஷரே முதல் சட்டம்.
mixed.exp: Practiced across India not just South (1 wrong). Associated with temple worship (✓). Princely states first legislated, not British directly (3 wrong). Only 2 is correct.

mixed.q:
The 'Permanent Settlement' (1793) — which are correct?
1. Created hereditary zamindars as landowners.
2. Revenue was permanently fixed.
3. Introduced in all provinces of British India.
mixed.qt: 1. वंशानुगत जमींदार उत्पन्न किए। 2. राजस्व स्थायी रूप से तय किया। 3. सभी प्रांतों में लागू।
mixed.exp: Permanent Settlement created hereditary zamindars (✓) and fixed revenue permanently (✓). But it was introduced only in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa — NOT all provinces (3 wrong).
Swaraj Party was founded by Motilal Nehru and C.R. (Chitta Ranjan) Das in 1923 to contest elections and obstruct the legislative councils from within.

mixed.q: The 'August Offer' (1940) by Lord Linlithgow proposed:
opts: Dominion status after WWII + Indian participation in war council
mixed.exp: The August Offer (8 Aug 1940) promised Dominion status after WWII, expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council to include more Indians, and establishment of a war advisory council — rejected by Congress.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

mixed.q: The Preamble was amended by which Amendment?
mixed.exp: 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

mixed.q: Right to Education (Art 21A) was inserted by:
mixed.exp: 86th Amendment Act (2002) inserted Art 21A — free compulsory education for children 6-14 years.
Judicial Review (courts reviewing laws against the Constitution) is borrowed from the USA.
Originally 10 duties (42nd Amendment 1976); an 11th added by 86th Amendment (2002).

mixed.q: The Constitution came into force on:
mixed.exp: Adopted 26 November 1949; came into force 26 January 1950 — celebrated as Republic Day.
Dr B.R. Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee — called Father of the Constitution.
Art 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) allows moving SC directly for Fundamental Rights. Ambedkar called it 'heart and soul'.

mixed.q: DPSP are contained in which Part?
mixed.exp: DPSP are in Part IV of the Constitution (Articles 36-51).
Rajya Sabha is a permanent House — it cannot be dissolved. One-third retire every two years.
Lok Sabha has 543 elected seats.

mixed.qt: தகவல் அறியும் உரிமை சட்டம் இயற்றப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
mixed.exp: Right to Information (RTI) Act was passed in 2005.

mixed.q: Chief Justice of India is appointed by:
mixed.exp: CJI is appointed by the President under Art 124(2), conventionally on the outgoing CJI's recommendation.

mixed.q: Minimum age for Rajya Sabha membership:
mixed.exp: Minimum age for Rajya Sabha is 30 years (Article 84).

mixed.q: Anti-Defection Law is in which Schedule?
mixed.qt: கட்சி தாவல் தடை சட்டம் எந்த அட்டவணையில்?
mixed.exp: Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment 1985) contains the Anti-Defection Law.

mixed.q: Finance Commission is constituted under Article:
mixed.exp: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, constituted by the President every five years.

mixed.q: Oath to President is administered by:
mixed.exp: CJI (or senior-most available judge) administers the oath to the President under Article 60.
Quorum = 1/10th of total membership (55 members).
Election Commission established 25 January 1950 under Article 324.

opts: Right to Life and Personal Liberty
mixed.exp: Art 21: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law.
Currently 22 officially recognised languages in the Eighth Schedule.

mixed.q: Emergency under Article 356 is known as:
mixed.exp: Article 356 provides for President's Rule (State Emergency) when state constitutional machinery fails.

mixed.q: Right to Property was removed from FDRs by:
mixed.exp: 44th Amendment (1978) removed Right to Property from FDRs and made it a legal right under Art 300A.

mixed.q: Speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by:
mixed.exp: Speaker is elected by Lok Sabha members from among themselves (Article 93).

mixed.q: Governor of a State is appointed by:
mixed.exp: Governor is appointed by the President under Article 155.

mixed.q: Money Bills can be introduced only in:
mixed.exp: Money Bills (Article 110) can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha.
Art 72: President can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions — including in death sentence cases.

mixed.q: Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in:
mixed.qt: திட்டக் கமிஷன் NITI ஆயோக்காக மாற்றப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
mixed.exp: NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

mixed.q: Maximum gap between two Parliamentary sessions:
mixed.qt: இரண்டு நாடாளுமன்ற கூட்டங்களுக்கு இடையேயான அதிகபட்ச இடைவெளி?
mixed.exp: Article 85: no more than 6 months between two parliamentary sessions.

mixed.q: Minimum age to become President of India:
mixed.exp: Minimum age to become President: 35 years (Article 58).

mixed.q:
DPSP statements:
1. Justiciable.
2. Part IV (Art 36-51).
3. Aim at welfare state.
mixed.qt:
DPSP:
1. நீதியில் நடைமுறைப்படுத்தலாம்.
2. பகுதி IV (36-51).
3. நல அரசு நோக்கம்.
mixed.exp: DPSPs are non-justiciable (1 wrong). In Part IV Art 36-51 (✓). Aim at welfare state (✓).
Public Order (Entry 1) is a State List subject.
73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj, adding Part IX and 11th Schedule.

mixed.qt: குடியரசுத் தலைவரை பதவி நீக்கம் செய்யும் சட்டப்பிரிவு?
mixed.exp: Article 61 provides the procedure for impeachment of the President.
Estimates Committee examines future estimates; PAC examines past expenditure.

mixed.q: Writ that orders a public authority to perform a duty:
mixed.exp: Mandamus ('we command') orders a public official to perform a mandatory duty they failed to perform.
Zero Hour starts at 12 noon — MPs raise urgent matters without prior notice. Not mentioned in Constitution.
Kesavananda Bharati v Kerala (1973) — SC held Parliament cannot amend the 'basic structure' of the Constitution.

mixed.q: Fundamental Duties were added by the:
mixed.exp: 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Art 51A) based on Swaran Singh Committee.
Arts 25-28: Right to Freedom of Religion — conscience, manage religious affairs, no tax for religion, no religious instruction in state schools.

mixed.q: New states can be created by Parliament under:
mixed.qt: புதிய மாநிலங்கள் நாடாளுமன்றத்தால் எந்த சட்டப்பிரிவின் கீழ் உருவாக்கப்படும்?
mixed.exp: Article 3 empowers Parliament (by simple majority) to create new states, alter boundaries and names.

mixed.q: Residuary powers in India belong to:
mixed.exp: Unlike USA (residuary to states), in India residuary powers belong to the Union/Parliament.

mixed.q: CAG of India is appointed by:
mixed.exp: CAG appointed by President under Art 148. Audits all government accounts.
VP elected by members of both Houses of Parliament assembled in a joint meeting (Art 66).

mixed.q: Article 3 vs Article 368 — creating a new state requires:
mixed.qt: புதிய மாநிலம் உருவாக்க Art 3 vs Art 368?
opts: Simple majority of Parliament + Presidential assent
mixed.exp: Art 3 requires only a simple majority in Parliament + Presidential assent (not special majority under Art 368). States' consent is not required.
74th Amendment gave constitutional status to municipalities, adding Part IX-A and 12th Schedule.

opts: Legislature doing indirectly what it cannot do directly
mixed.exp: Prevents a legislature from encroaching on another's jurisdiction by framing a law differently.

mixed.q: National Emergency (Art 352) can be proclaimed due to:
opts: War, external aggression, or armed rebellion
mixed.exp: Art 352 covers war, external aggression, or armed rebellion (44th Amendment changed 'internal disturbance' to 'armed rebellion').

mixed.q: Cultural and Educational Rights of minorities (Arts 29-30):
mixed.exp: Art 29: conserve language/culture. Art 30: minorities' right to establish and administer educational institutions.

mixed.q: The President can issue ordinances when:
mixed.qt: குடியரசுத் தலைவர் அவசர ஆணை பிறப்பிக்கும் நேரம்?
mixed.exp: Under Art 123, President can issue ordinances only when both Houses are not in session.

opts: Tribal areas administration in NE India
mixed.exp: 6th Schedule: administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram through Autonomous District Councils.

mixed.q: High Court judges are appointed by:
opts: President in consultation with CJI and Governor
mixed.exp: HC judges appointed by President under Art 217 in consultation with CJI and concerned state Governor.

mixed.q: India follows which type of government?
mixed.exp: India follows Parliamentary (Westminster) system — executive responsible to legislature.
Habeas Corpus ('you may have the body') directs authorities to produce a detained person before court.
Question Hour = first hour of every Parliamentary sitting where ministers answer members' questions.

opts: Restored rights curtailed by 42nd Amendment; amended Emergency provisions
mixed.exp: 44th Amendment (1978) restored several rights curtailed by 42nd Amendment and added emergency safeguards.

mixed.q: The SC's 'Constitutional Morality' principle was invoked in:
mixed.exp: Navtej Singh Johar v Union of India (2018) — decriminalised consensual homosexuality — extensively invoked constitutional morality.

opts: Quash the order of a lower court acting beyond jurisdiction
mixed.exp: Certiorari quashes the order of a lower court/tribunal that has acted beyond its jurisdiction or against principles of natural justice.

mixed.q: The 'Doctrine of Ultra Vires' in constitutional law means:
mixed.exp: Ultra Vires ('beyond powers') = an act performed by a body/authority that exceeds the powers granted to it by law or the Constitution.

mixed.q: Under the Constitution, which is a 'state' for Art 12 (definition of state for Fundamental Rights)?
mixed.qt: அடிப்படை உரிமைகளுக்கு சட்டப்பிரிவு 12 கீழ் 'மாநிலம்' என்பதில் அடங்குவது?
opts: Government of India, Parliament, State Govts, Local bodies + instrumentalities of State
mixed.exp: Art 12: 'State' includes Government of India, Parliament, state governments and legislatures, and all local or other authorities under the control of the government or funded by it.

mixed.q: The 'Panchayat Extension to Scheduled Areas' (PESA) Act 1996 extends:
opts: Panchayat Raj to all tribal areas
Gram Sabha powers to Schedule V areas, giving tribals self-governance
mixed.exp: PESA (1996) extended Panchayati Raj provisions to Schedule V (tribal) areas in 10 states, empowering Gram Sabhas with self-governance, traditional rights, and control over resources.

mixed.q: Which of the following has original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
opts: Disputes between the Union and one or more states
mixed.exp: Under Art 131, SC has original jurisdiction in disputes between the Union and states, or between two or more states — exclusively. This cannot be heard by any other court.

mixed.q: The President of India cannot dissolve:
mixed.exp: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha but NOT the Rajya Sabha — as it is a permanent House. State Assemblies can be dissolved by the Governor on CM's advice.

mixed.q: 'Comptroller and Auditor General' (CAG) — which is correct?
opts: CAG is the guardian of public purse; reports to Parliament; independent of Executive
mixed.exp: CAG is the supreme audit institution — independent of executive, submits reports to Parliament/State Legislatures, and guards the public purse.

opts: Device to raise an urgent public issue by interrupting House business
mixed.exp: Adjournment Motion is a device to draw attention to a definite matter of urgent public importance by adjourning business of the House — allowed only in Lok Sabha.

mixed.q: 'Financial Emergency' under Art 360 can be proclaimed when:
opts: When financial stability or credit of India or any part thereof is threatened
mixed.exp: Art 360: Financial Emergency when the financial stability or credit of India or any state is threatened. Never been proclaimed in India so far.

opts: Freedom of speech inside Parliament without liability in any court
mixed.exp: Parliamentary privileges include freedom of speech inside Parliament (protected from court proceedings), right to publish debates, and right to punish outsiders for breach of privilege.

mixed.q: The 'Right to Privacy' was declared a Fundamental Right by the SC in:
mixed.qt: 'தனியுரிமை உரிமை' அடிப்படை உரிமை என தீர்ப்பளிக்கப்பட்ட ஆண்டு?
mixed.exp: In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017), a 9-judge SC bench unanimously held that Right to Privacy is a Fundamental Right under Art 21.

mixed.q: The 'No-Confidence Motion' can be moved only in:
mixed.exp: A No-Confidence Motion (censure motion against Council of Ministers) can only be moved in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha.

mixed.q: 'NOTA' (None of the Above) was introduced in Indian elections in:
mixed.exp: NOTA was introduced in Indian elections in 2013 following the Supreme Court order in People's Union for Civil Liberties v Union of India (2013).
Gram Nyayalayas (village courts) were established under the Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008 to provide cheap and quick justice at grassroots level.

mixed.q: 'Token Money Bill' vs 'Appropriation Bill' — which is correct?
mixed.qt: 'டோக்கன் மணி பில்' vs 'திரும்பளிப்பு மசோதா' — சரியான விளக்கம்?
opts: Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from Consolidated Fund; token bills are for small grants in lieu
Token bills are for rural areas only
Appropriation Bill is only for defence
mixed.exp: Appropriation Bill authorises the government to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund for approved expenditure. It gives formal legal authority to government spending.

mixed.q: 'Comptroller' role of CAG differs from 'Auditor' role in that:
opts: Comptroller role (for Union) was eliminated; CAG now mainly audits state/central accounts
The Comptroller role was formally abandoned; CAG now mainly functions as auditor
Comptroller role applies to state governments only
mixed.exp: CAG's comptroller function (pre-authorising government expenditure) was abolished in 1976 when the Consolidated Fund was changed. CAG now mainly functions as auditor, not pre-auditor.

opts: Division of taxing powers and expenditure responsibilities between Centre and States
mixed.exp: Fiscal federalism = constitutional division of taxing powers (Union List, State List, concurrent) and expenditure responsibilities between Central and State governments, with Finance Commission managing transfers.

mixed.q:
Constitutional language provisions:
1. Hindi in Devanagari = official Union language.
2. English only for 15 years.
3. States may adopt own language.
mixed.qt:
1. தேவநாகரி இந்தி ஆட்சி மொழி.
2. ஆங்கிலம் 15 ஆண்டுகள் மட்டும்.
3. மாநிலங்கள் சொந்த மொழி ஏற்கலாம்.
mixed.exp: All correct. Art 343: Hindi official. English extended indefinitely by Official Languages Act 1963. Art 345: states can adopt own language.

mixed.q:
Governor's absolute discretionary powers:
1. Sending Art 356 report.
2. Reserving Bill for President.
3. Seeking info from CM.
4. Returning non-money bill.
mixed.exp: Sending Art 356 report and reserving a Bill (Art 201) are absolute discretionary. Seeking info (Art 167) and returning bill are done on CM's advice.

mixed.q:
9th Schedule:
1. Laws completely immune from judicial review.
2. Added by First Amendment.
3. IR Coelho case (2007): violations of basic structure can be reviewed.
mixed.qt:
9வது அட்டவணை:
1. முழு நீதி மறுஆய்வு விலக்கு.
2. முதல் திருத்தத்தால் சேர்க்கப்பட்டது.
3. IR Coelho தீர்ப்பு: மறுஆய்வு சாத்தியம்.
mixed.exp: 9th Schedule added by 1st Amendment (✓). IR Coelho (2007): laws after 24 April 1973 violating basic structure CAN be reviewed — NOT immune (1 wrong).

mixed.q:
Article 356 safeguards:
1. Parliamentary approval within 2 months.
2. Extension beyond 1 year only if Emergency is in operation.
3. SR Bommai (1994): President's Rule subject to judicial review.
mixed.qt:
1. 2 மாதத்தில் நாடாளுமன்றம் அங்கீகரிக்க வேண்டும்.
2. 1 ஆண்டுக்கு மேல் நீட்டிக்க அவசரநிலை தேவை.
3. SR Bommai: நீதி மறுஆய்வுக்கு உட்பட்டது.
mixed.exp: All three correct. 2-month approval (44th Amendment). Beyond 1 year needs national emergency. SR Bommai (1994) made it judicially reviewable.

mixed.q: Art 368 amendments affecting federal structure require:
mixed.qt: சட்டப்பிரிவு 368 கீழ் கூட்டாட்சி கட்டமைப்பை பாதிக்கும் திருத்தங்களுக்கு?
opts: Special majority + ratification by at least half state legislatures
mixed.exp: Federal structure amendments need special majority (2/3 of present and voting + majority of total membership) PLUS ratification by at least half state legislatures.
Art 20(2): no person can be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.

mixed.q: Which are Constitutional Bodies (created directly by Constitution)?
opts: Election Commission, UPSC, CAG, Finance Commission
mixed.exp: EC (Art 324), UPSC (Art 315), CAG (Art 148), Finance Commission (Art 280) — all constitutional. NHRC, CBI, SEBI are statutory.

mixed.q: Maneka Gandhi case (1978) expanded Art 21 by holding:
mixed.qt: மானேகா காந்தி வழக்கு (1978) சட்டப்பிரிவு 21 ஐ விரிவுபடுத்தியது எப்படி?
opts: Art 21 limited to mere physical existence
'Procedure established by law' must be just, fair, and reasonable
mixed.exp: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India (1978) held that 'procedure established by law' must be just, fair, and reasonable — vastly expanding Art 21's scope.
Both religious and linguistic minorities have Art 30 rights. TMA Pai Foundation case (2002) clarified minority status is determined state-wise.

mixed.q: Under Art 143, President can seek SC advisory opinion on:
mixed.qt: சட்டப்பிரிவு 143 கீழ் குடியரசுத் தலைவர் SC ஆலோசனை கோரலாம்?
opts: Question of law or fact of public importance
mixed.exp: Art 143 allows President to refer any question of law or fact of public importance to SC for advisory opinion.

mixed.q:
Consolidated Fund of India — which are correct?
1. No money without Appropriation Act.
2. Includes revenues, loans, repayments.
3. CAG audits all expenditure from it.
mixed.qt:
1. திரும்பளிப்பு சட்டம் இல்லாமல் பணம் எடுக்க முடியாது.
2. வருவாய், கடன்கள் அடங்கும்.
3. CAG தணிக்கை செய்யும்.
mixed.exp: All three correct. Art 114: Appropriation Act needed. Art 266: includes revenues/loans. CAG audits all govt expenditure.

opts: Government has final say on HC judge appointment
SC collegium recommendation is binding for SC judges
CJI alone decides all SC appointments
mixed.exp: Second Judges Case (1993): collegium's recommendation is binding on the President for SC appointments.

mixed.q:
73rd Amendment — which are mandatory?
1. Gram Sabha.
2. Three-tier structure.
3. SC/ST reservation proportional to population.
4. Five-year term.
mixed.exp: All four are mandatory: Gram Sabha, three-tier structure, SC/ST reservations, and five-year term.

opts: President acts at will without advice
Certain officials hold office at the President's pleasure
mixed.exp: Art 310: certain high officials hold posts at pleasure of President/Governor — can be dismissed subject to constitutional safeguards.

mixed.qt: இந்தியாவிற்குள் மட்டுமே அமைந்த மிக உயரமான சிகரம்?
mixed.exp: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) on Sikkim-Nepal border. K2 is in Pakistan-administered territory.

mixed.q: Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
mixed.exp: 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.
Kosi River floods frequently due to heavy silt deposits that shift its course.
Sundarbans — world's largest mangrove forest — is in West Bengal (also extends into Bangladesh).
Ganga (2,525 km) is the longest river entirely in India.
Indira Point (Pygmalion Point) in Great Nicobar Island. Kanyakumari is the southernmost mainland point.
Thar Desert in Rajasthan is the largest desert in India, 7th largest in the world.

mixed.q: State with longest coastline in India:
mixed.exp: Gujarat has the longest coastline (~1,600 km).

mixed.q: Western Ghats are also known as:
mixed.exp: Western Ghats = Sahyadri range, running parallel to the western coast.
Brahmaputra originates from Chemayungdung glacier near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet.
Chilika Lake in Odisha is Asia's largest brackish water lagoon and a Ramsar Wetland Site.
Leh is the capital of the Union Territory of Ladakh.
Vembanad Lake in Kerala is the longest lake; Wular Lake in J&K is the largest freshwater lake.

mixed.q: Silent Valley National Park is in:
mixed.exp: Silent Valley NP is in Palakkad district, Kerala — famous for undisturbed tropical rainforest.

mixed.q: Indian Standard Time (IST) corresponds to which longitude?
mixed.exp: IST corresponds to 82.5°E longitude, passing through Mirzapur, UP.

mixed.q: The Sundarbans delta is formed by:
mixed.exp: Sundarbans delta formed by Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers emptying into Bay of Bengal.

mixed.q: Largest Union Territory of India by area:
mixed.exp: Ladakh is the largest UT of India by area (59,146 sq km).
Narmada River originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh.

mixed.qt: பால்க் நீர்ச்சந்தி இந்தியாவை எந்த நாட்டிலிருந்து பிரிக்கிறது?
mixed.exp: Palk Strait separates southeastern India (Tamil Nadu) from Sri Lanka.

mixed.q: Majuli island is in which river?
mixed.exp: Majuli — world's largest river island — is in the Brahmaputra, Assam.
Konkan Coast extends from Mumbai (Daman) to Goa along the western coast.

mixed.q: City on the banks of Sabarmati:
mixed.exp: Ahmedabad is on the Sabarmati River. Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram is here.

mixed.q: Loktak Lake (NE India's largest freshwater lake) is in:
mixed.exp: Loktak Lake in Manipur has floating 'phumdis' and the world's only floating national park.

mixed.qt: கிழக்குத் தொடர்ச்சி மலை எந்த மாநிலங்கள் வழியாக?
mixed.exp: Eastern Ghats are discontinuous ranges through Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha.

mixed.q: State with maximum forest cover in India:
mixed.qt: இந்தியாவில் மிக அதிக வனப்பகுதி கொண்ட மாநிலம்?
mixed.exp: Arunachal Pradesh has maximum forest cover by area; Mizoram leads by percentage of total area.

mixed.q: Nilgiris are at the junction of:
mixed.exp: Nilgiri Hills are at the junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka.

mixed.q: Coromandel Coast gets rainfall primarily during:
mixed.qt: கோரமண்டல் கரை முக்கியமாக எப்போது மழை பெறுகிறது?
mixed.exp: Coromandel Coast (east coast of TN and southern AP) gets most rain during the Northeast monsoon.
Kunchikal Falls in Karnataka (455 m) is the highest waterfall in India.

mixed.q:
Western Ghats statements:
1. Older than Himalayas.
2. Parallel to western coast.
3. UNESCO Biodiversity Hotspot 2012.
mixed.qt:
1. இமயமலையை விட பழமையானவை.
2. மேற்கு கரைக்கு இணையாக.
3. யுனெஸ்கோ 2012.
mixed.exp: All correct. Ancient block mountains (Archean) > Himalayan age. Run parallel to west coast. UNESCO 2012.
Cauvery → Talakaveri, Coorg. Narmada → Amarkantak. Godavari → Trimbakeshwar. Krishna → Mahabaleshwar.
Bhabar = narrow gravel/pebble belt at Himalayan foothills. Rivers flow underground here, re-emerge in Terai.

mixed.q: Indian monsoon is primarily caused by:
opts: Differential heating of land and sea; ITCZ shift
mixed.exp: Indian monsoon caused by differential heating of land/sea, northward shift of ITCZ in summer, and Coriolis effect.

mixed.q: Deccan Trap formation was caused by:
mixed.exp: Deccan Traps formed by massive volcanic eruptions around 65 million years ago (end of Cretaceous).
Narmada, Tapi, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri are Peninsular rivers originating in the Deccan.

mixed.q: Western Disturbances in India originate over:
mixed.exp: Western Disturbances originate as extratropical cyclones over the Mediterranean Sea, bringing winter rain to NW India.

mixed.q: Rain Shadow area of Western Ghats:
mixed.exp: The Deccan Plateau (leeward/eastern side) is in the rain shadow — much drier than the windward western side.

mixed.q: Soil best suited for cotton cultivation in India:
mixed.qt: இந்தியாவில் பருத்தி சாகுபடிக்கு மிகவும் ஏற்ற மண் வகை?
mixed.exp: Black soil (Regur) found in Deccan Plateau — high clay content, moisture retention — ideal for cotton.

mixed.q: Kaziranga National Park is associated with:
mixed.exp: Kaziranga NP in Assam is home to ~2/3 of world's Indian One-horned Rhinoceros. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Project Tiger launched 1 April 1973 by PM Indira Gandhi at Jim Corbett National Park.
Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (AP/Telangana) is largest by area (3,568 sq km).
The Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta is the world's largest river delta.
Chhota Nagpur Plateau (Jharkhand) — rich in coal, iron ore, manganese, mica, bauxite.

mixed.qt: மிக உயரமான சிகரங்களை கொண்ட இமயமலைத் தொடர்?
mixed.exp: Great Himalayas (Himadri) is northernmost and highest — contains Everest, Kangchenjunga, etc.
Terai = marshy, swampy lowland belt south of the Bhabar, at Himalayan foothills. Rich biodiversity.
Lakshadweep = coral atolls in the Arabian Sea. India's smallest UT with 36 islands.

mixed.q: Malabar Coast refers to the coast of:
mixed.exp: Malabar Coast = southwestern coast of India, primarily Kerala and parts of Karnataka.
India's EEZ extends 200 nautical miles from the baseline, giving sovereign rights over natural resources.

mixed.q:
Indo-Gangetic Plain alluvium types:
1. Formed by Himalayan river deposits.
2. Bhangar and Khadar are two types.
3. Khadar is older; Bhangar is newer.
mixed.qt:
1. ஹிமாலய நதிகளின் படிவால் உருவானது.
2. பங்கர் மற்றும் கதார் — இரண்டு வகைகள்.
3. கதார் பழைய வண்டல்; பங்கர் புதியது.
mixed.exp: Formed by Himalayan rivers (✓). Bhangar and Khadar are alluvium types (✓). But Bhangar is OLD; Khadar is NEW — Statement 3 is reversed.

mixed.q: Which soil has highest water retention?
mixed.qt: மிக அதிக நீர் தேக்கும் திறன் கொண்ட மண் வகை?
mixed.exp: Black cotton soil (Regur) has highest water retention — swells when wet, cracks when dry.

opts: Kerala, Karnataka, and parts of Maharashtra and Odisha
mixed.exp: Laterite soil is found mainly in high rainfall areas with alternating wet and dry seasons — Kerala, Karnataka, parts of Maharashtra, Odisha, and some hill regions.
Blue Revolution refers to the development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in India, aiming to increase fish production.

mixed.q: The 'Kaziranga' National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for which primary reason?
mixed.qt: காஸிரங்கா தேசிய பூங்கா UNESCO அங்கீகாரம் பெற்ற முக்கிய காரணம்?
opts: Major population of Indian one-horned rhinoceros
mixed.exp: Kaziranga NP was inscribed as UNESCO WHS in 1985 primarily for its extraordinary density of Indian one-horned rhinoceros (~2/3 of world population).

mixed.q: Which is India's longest national highway?
mixed.exp: NH-44 (formerly NH-7) from Srinagar to Kanyakumari is India's longest national highway at ~3,745 km.

mixed.q: 'Project Snow Leopard' was launched to conserve:
opts: Snow leopards and their Himalayan/Trans-Himalayan habitat
mixed.exp: Project Snow Leopard (2009) was launched to protect snow leopards and their Himalayan and Trans-Himalayan habitats in 5 states: J&K, HP, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh.

opts: They act as coastal protection, carbon sink, nursery for marine life
mixed.exp: Mangroves protect coasts from storms and tsunamis, serve as carbon sinks, provide nursery habitats for marine species, and support coastal livelihoods.

mixed.q: The 'Deccan plateau' is bounded on the north by:
mixed.qt: டெக்கான் பீடபூமி வடக்கில் எந்த மலைத்தொடர்களால் எல்லையிடப்படுகிறது?
mixed.exp: The Deccan Plateau is bounded on the north by the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

mixed.q: India shares its longest border with which country?
mixed.qt: இந்தியா மிக நீண்ட எல்லையை பகிர்ந்து கொள்ளும் நாடு?
mixed.exp: India shares its longest border with Bangladesh (~4,156 km), followed by China (~3,488 km), Pakistan (~3,323 km), Nepal, and others.
National Waterway 1 (Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system) extends from Haldia (Kolkata) to Allahabad (Prayagraj), total 1,620 km.

mixed.q: The Godavari River is also known as:

mixed.q: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana aims to:
mixed.exp: PMAY (2015) — affordable housing for all eligible families, Housing for All mission.

mixed.q: 'Base Erosion and Profit Shifting' (BEPS) is about:

mixed.exp: PM-Kisan (2019) provides ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000 each to small and marginal farmers owning up to 2 hectares.
